SPECIFCATIONS The cars are equipped with an electronic system known as the ALFA CODE that acts as an engine immobiliser. The ALFA CODE system allows the engine to start by means of the Engine NCM only after receiving a secret code memorised previously. SPECIFIC FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM The second generation Code system is integrated in the Body Computer Node (NBC). COMPOSITION The ALFA CODE system comprises 5 basic elements (in addition to the Body Computer which acts as control unit): C CAN line for dialogue with BCN and ECN bidirectional serial line for recovery ( W line) two to eight electronic keys containing a transponder with a secret code; an aerial which reads the code contained in the key transponders; the NCM for petrol engines and for electronic diesel pumps or the Diesel Valve Electronic Driver (D._E.D.) 1 - NBC 2 - ECN 3 - Aerial 4 - Key OPERATION INTRODUCTION The ALFA CODE allows engine control management to be commenced by the NCM by coded dialogue between the NBC and NCM during the pre-starting stage. After the ignition is switched on, the NCM sends a request code to the NBC which responds only after recognizing (via the aerial) a known electronic key inserted in the ignition switch. If the secret code contained in the response is valid, the NCM continues with the usual engine control activity, allowing the engine to be started. The NCM can memorise the secret code only by means of a particular procedure. The ALFA CODE function is also guaranteed in the case of malfunction of the other NBC functions. After recognising an enabled transponder, the ALFA CODE switches off any alarm system. INTERACTION OF ALFA CODE WITH THE KEY Each key contains a transponder with the IDENTIFIER CODE and the SECRET CODE. As soon as the ignition is switched on (+15), the transponder sends the identifier to the ALFA CODE which, recognising it as one of the enabled ones, proceeds with the strategy for recognising the cytographic transponder If the identifier is not recognised, the procedure aborts, preventing the engine from being started. The cryptographic transponder is recognised by means of a challenge-response algorithm with exchange of encrypted code. The code recognition time does not exceed 160 ms per attempt. The ALFA CODE attempts for 1 second to acquire the transponder. DIALOGUE BETWEEN ENGINE CONTROL NODE AND ALFA CODE The dialogue between ALFA CODE (NBC) and NCM takes place on the C-CAN under normal operating conditions. Each exchange of information between ALFA CODE and the NCM (the ALFA CODE never interrogates the NCM, but only answers after a request from the latter). When the ignition is switched on, the flow of operations involving code exchange between the ALFA CODE and the NCM depends on the state (virgin or memorised) of the engine management control unit. If the NCM is virgin, the procedure involves the fix code request to the ALFA CODE: in this way, the NCM learns and memorises the secret code. This procedure is called CODE RECORDING. If the NCM is programmed, the procedure involves checking that the fix code memorised in the engine control unit is the same as that memorised in the ALFA CODE (NBC): the NCM asks the NBC for the secret code and compares it with its own. This procedure is called CODE VERIFY 1 - Key on 2 - NCM initialisation 3 - Memorized/virgin NCM status 4 - Memorization successfully completed ? 5 - ENABLE ENGINE MANAGEMENT = the flow of software continues with the management of the engine management. 6 - PROHIBIT ENGINE MANAGEMENT = activates a timer which creates a dely to only enable a new procedure after 0 - 600 secs. It is necessary to remove and and restore +15. If a timer is not available (with + 30) it will be necessary to wait 0 - 600 secs in key on. After this it is possible to carry out a new procedure with a KEY OFF and KEY ON. 7 - Is the secret code valid ? 8 - SEE POINT 6 9 - SEE POINT 5 A - CODE VERIFY B - CODE RECORDING Code recording The CODE RECORDING procedure is the memorisation of the fix code in the engine control unit. Only after memorising the identifiers, secret code and fix code, the ALFA CODE is ready to meet the request to transmit a code from the NCM which is still virgin. After 'power on', the engine control unit initialises its software and, if it is virgin, asks for the fix code. If the ALFA CODE is not virgin, it will respond by sending the fix code, but only after recognising an enabled key. If it is a disabled (unknown) key or there is no key, the ALFA CODE does not respond. When the ALFA CODE is virgin and there is no transponder in the aerial and a a FIX code request is sent from the NCM to the ALFA CODE, the ALFA CODE does not respond. Code verify This is the standard procedure which is repeated during the life the car whenever the driver inserts the key in the ignition switch and turns the ignition on (+15) (= KEY ON): this procedure allows engine starting if the inserted key is enabled. The code verify procedure continues even wne the driver turns the key to +50 (CRANKING). After the key is on KEY ON (+15), the ALFA CODE recognises whether the transponder in the key is one of the enabled ones. At the same time, with the key on +15 or +50, the NCM initialises its software to verify whether a fix code has already been memorised. If it has, it will send a (FIX code request) to the ALFA CODE. In response to this request, the ALFA CODE will send the fix code, encrypted by the Minikrypt, to the engine management control unit, only if the transponder has been recognised as enabled. If the ALFA CODE receives further (FIX code) requests, it only reads the transponder in the aerial again before responding to the NCM if there are visible signs of possible manipulation (see later). If the result of the transponder recognition is negative (incorrect transponder, no transponder in the aerial, etc.), the ALFA CODE will send the code (incorrect transponder or no transponder) to the engine management control unit. If the ALFA CODE is virgin and the NCM sends a FIX code request, the ALFA CODE, after recognising a transponder, responds by sending an encrypted virgin NBC recognised transponder code, encrypted by the Minikrypt. METHOD OF USING C-CAN OR RECOVERY W LINE Communication between the NBC and NCM takes place by default on the C-CAN line; if the C-CAN is faulty, the recovery strategy is as follows: C-CAN faulty the ECN passes on to recovery on the W serial line, requesting the code from the BCN: if the outcome is positive, starting is permitted if there are also problems on the W line, after re-transmission attempts, the NCM passes on to recovery from the accelerator pedal or the diagnostic instrument. The recovery strategy is mainly managed by the NCM, which acts as a master unit during communication: the NBC acts as the slave unit and must therefore always be ready to respond to code requests from the C-CAN and W serial line. Communication on c-can The communication between Body Computer and NCM is achieved by the following two CAN messages: IMMO CODE REQUEST (immo code request) IMMO CODE RESPONSE (immo code response) The IMMO CODE REQUEST is sent by the NMC and received by the NBC. The IMMO CODE RESPONSE is sent by the NBC and received by the NCM. Communication on w line If, because of a malfunction on the CAN network, you move on to the recovery condition, the exchange of codes between NCM and NBC takes place on the W serial line. This code exchange takes place only for the CODE VERIFY procedure: it is therefore not possible to carry out a CODE RECORDING on the W line. The data exchange on the serial line takes place in the same way as on the C-CAN network: the NCM control unit is master of the communication, while the NBC responds to the requests received from the NCM. Two messages travel on the serial line, the IMMO CODE REQUEST and the IMMO CODE RESPONSE. VERIFYING W LINE ELECTRICAL CONNECTION As the dialogue on the W line only takes place in the case of recovery, an ERROR condition would only be recognised at the time of use, so the end customer would not be able to move the car. A strategy of verifying the W serial line is therefore introduced in order to diagnose the line itself. PROTECTION CODES The ALFA CODE function is implemented via the exchange of secret codes between the various subsystems (keys, NBC, engine management unit). UNIVERSAL CODE: this is the code which the ALFA CODE, not yet programmed, sends to the NCM when it has recognised the presence of a transponder in the key. The ALFA CODE warning light comes on at a frequency of 1.6 Hz and duty cycle of 50%. The flashing of the light explains that the system is correctly connected and working, but the car is not protected by a code. IMMO CODE: This is the basic code from which the secret code and fix code are obtained. An automatically generated immmo code is associated with each car. All the other secret codes used by the ALFA CODE function are generated from the IMMO CODE. SECRET CODE: This is the code resident in the transponder. It is memorised in the transponders contained in the car keys at the time of programming the transponders, and in the ALFA CODE at the time of programming the keys at the end of the line. FIX CODE: This is memorised in the ALFA CODE at the time of end-of-line programming. ELECTRONIC CODE (PIN): This is obtained from the fix code and is stamped on the CODE CARD which is delivered to the car's owner; it is a 5-digit decimal code (0 is not permitted). It is used to access, in a protected manner, the NBC memory in order to re-programme or programme new remote control keys and/or carry out particular diagnostic functions. It is also used in the procedure of recovery from accelerator pedal described in the engine control unit specification. IDENTIFIER: It is resident in the transponder and is different for each transponder. It is memorised in the ALFA CODE during the programming procedure. The ALFA CODE manages a table of enabled identifications and one for disabled identifications. DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPONENTS ALFA CODE FUNCTION IN THE NBC Specifications The ALFA CODE on the 147 is a function of the BCN The main functions of the ALFA CODE are: to recognise the introduction and rotation of a key in the ignition switch (+15); to de-activate the alarm after recognition of an enabled key; to emit an electromagnetic field to read the key's transponder; to send the random code to the transponder; to receive the cryptographic code emitted by the key; to memorise up to 8 identifiers; to memorise the secret code; to manage a list of a maximum of 8 enabled identifiers; to manage a list of at least 16 permanently disabled identifiers; to manage the C-CAN line to the engine management control unit; to manage the lighting up of the warning light on the panel by dialoguing with the NQS; to carry out self-diagnosis. Aerial Characteristics Toroidal aerial Ohm value= 40 Ohm Composition The aerial assembly consists of a 131 coil toroidal reel aerial with built-in connector on the aerial body. The connecting wiring to the BCN is integrated in the dashboard wiring loom. Operation The aerial is supplied by the NBC to energise the key's transponder. As the aerial needs to be as close as possible to the transponder (for electromagnetic immunity, its small size and the limited range of the transponder), it is attached axially to the ignition switch. 1 - CODE aerial 2 - Ignition switch IGNITION KEY Characteristics The mechanical key contains a cryptographic transponder in the handle. Operation When the key is inserted in the switch and the ignition is switched on (+15), the transponder is energized by the aerial and responds by emitting the secret code in a variable and encrypted way. The emission into the air has sufficient power to have high immunity to electromagnetic interference and a range such that it is received by the aerial mounted in the ignition switch. If the code is recognised as valid, the ALFA CODE sends the engine control unit, at the request of the latter, a coded signal that allows the engine to be started. Up to 8 keys can be programmed in the ALFA CODE. The keys are supplied 'already programmed' by the production factory. All the codes are then stored in a DATA BASE managed by the PARTS DIVISION. Therefore, when a new vehicle is handed over to a customer, the Service Network should not carry out any programming procedures. If a key is mislaid or additional keys are requested, this request should be passed on to the Parts Dept. following the procedures in the 'REPAIR PROCEDURES' section. 1 - Transponder KEY TRANSPONDER Specifcations The transponder contained in the key has the following coded in its memory: SECRET CODE, the same for each transponder in the same key kit; IDENTIFIER, different for each transponder produced; DATE OF PROGRAMMING the secret code The identifier differs from transponder to transponder to ensure that, even if duplicates are requested on the Network, there are not several transponders with the same identifier. Key programming The storage procedure is divided into two stages in sequence: the key transponders are stored in the ALFA CODE; the ALFA CODE manages storage of the fix code in the engine management control unit This second step is implemented automatically when the first is completed successfully at key on. Supply of key kits Transponders are sent to the manufacturer programmed with an identifier (different for each transponder). The key manufacturer generates an immo code, computes the codes (secret code, fix-code) and programmes the secret code and programming date into the key transponders. Once they are programmed, it printes a bar code onto a disposable label that contains the immo code, the key identifiers, the programming date, the key mechanical code and, if present, the remote control/alarm codes. The secret code in the kit keys is stored in the ALFA CODE during the end of line programming procedure. It is used in the cryptographic algorithm for key recognition. Programming a new body computer If the Body Computer is replaced, the ALFA CODE must be programmed with the secret code and the fix code of the vehicle in which it is installed. The database is accessed using the chassis number and the car immo code is obtained. The secret code and fix-code are obtained from this and programmed into the NBC. In the case of a new NBC, the enabled and disabled identifier tables are empty. Once the NBC has been installed in the car, a tester is used to store the key identifiers (see key programming). An ALFA CODE can only be programmed for a blank NBC by the ALFA ROMEO parts dept. Reprogramming the keys Reprogramming the keys enables the keys authorised to start the car to be memorised in the NBC. The new keys to be programmed and those already programmed will be inserted in the ignition switch to be recognised by the ALFA CODE which will memorise in the table of enabled identifiers those presented during the procedure, and will transfer from the latter table to the table of disabled identifiers those identifiers which have not been presented. Table of disabled keys If an enabled key is no longer available (lost, stolen or no longer working), the subsequent key programming procedure (for example necessary for memorising the new replacement key) should disable its operation. The ALFA CODE therefore manages a table in EEPROM which can contain the data relating to 16 disabled keys: the identifiers of the enabled keys not presented during the reprogramming procedures are transferred into this table. If the disabled keys table is full, any new key will replace the first key entered on the table. This table also permits traceability of the keys used on the car. Key reprogramming prodecure The minimum time for a KEY-ON during the storage procedure is 1 seconds. The key reprogramming procedure is carried out/guided by the Diagnostic/Test Instrument: this procedure is activated by access protected by the car's PIN. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: the diagnostic instrument instructs the NBC to initialize the key learning procedure. the operator enters the first key and requests learning from the NBC: the NBC reads the transponder after Key-on, verifies whether the secret code is correct and, if it is, learns the key's identifier. the operator repeats operation 2 for all the car's keys. once all the keys have been learnt, the diagnostic instrument instructs the BCN to memorise them permanently in EEPROM, in accordance with the following procedure: the BCN compares the learnt identifiers with those currently in memory the data of the keys memorised in EEPROM but not presented during learning, they are moved to the disabled keys table. the data of the learnt keys are memorised in the enabled keys table only if they are not already present in the disabled keys table. Up to a maximum of 8 enabled keys can be programmed. Deletion from memory of a lost key The procedure is the same as that described in the previous paragraph. All the keys owned must be presented; those not presented will be deleted, i.e. transferred into the table of disabled identifiers. A lost key may be deleted from memory at any time by a diagnostic/test instrument. The identifier of that key is transferred into the disabled keys table and will no longer be recognised. CODE CARD Composition This card contains the following: The emergency code (electronic code) which allows the car to be started with the EXAMINER or another diagnostic instrument or, in an emergency, with the accelerator pedal procedure. It is also used to programme the keys and remote controls with the EXAMINER. The mechanical code of the keys (mechanical code) identifies the mechanical profile of the key, and must be specified in the order to receive the key already cut. 1 - Electronic code 2 - Mechanical code Operation The 'electronic' emergency code is also used for diagnosis of the system and for other operations with the Examiner or another diagnostic instrument. Many of these operations (e.g. 'Programming Keys') can only be carried out after this code has been entered. Therefore before any operation, the Customer must be asked for the Code Card. The Code Card should not be left in the vehicle in case it is stolen: it should, however, be available for the emergency starting procedure described below. FAULT DIAGNOSIS The ALFA CODE function permits the possibility of carrying out self-diagnosis of the parts which make up the system. The NBC can identify and memorise in EEPROM the presence of the following malfunctions: Transponder: faulty or absent or with incorrect secret code deleted/disabled unknown/not memorised Transponder aerial: faulty electrical connection (open circuit, short circuit to earth or to battery) Active diagnosis By means of commands sent from the Tester it is possible to: Ask whether the ALFA CODE is: virgin (each time a key is inserted) programmed at the end of the line (each key a key is inserted) a replacement part (each time a key is inserted) virgin/programmed NCM link with NCM OK / KO Ask the number of keys programmed. Read one key at a time and know the following for each key: valid transponder if the key is programmed its position in the table if the secret code is valid the key ID Ask the number and identifier of the last key used Ask for the reading of all enabled keys Ask the number of enabled keys and the number of disabled keys Manually programme the keys through successive acquisitions with the effectiveness of the transponder being checked at each acquisition. It should be possible to recognize the presence of a transponder in the aerial and whether or not it is valid. Request current system status identified by: last key used is enabled and recognized the BC has received a code request from the engine management control unit the NCM is virgin the ALFA CODE is virgin BC is enabled to send the Minikrypt key the identifier of the last key used is present in the enabled keys table the identifier of the last key used is present in the disabled keys table the ALFA CODE has identified a tamper attempt at +15 Control CODE warning light activation/deactivation on the NQS Recovery procedure by accelerator pedal Whenever the customer wishes to start the engine and has problems with the ALFA CODE, the following procedure should be activated. The recovery procedure is an emergency procedure and allows the user to regain possession of the car if the key has been lost or damaged. By 'manual' entry of a sub-code (EMERGENCY CODE). The RECOVERY PROCEDURE can only be activated after the NCM has entered 'ENGINE IMMOBILIZED' status. The RECOVERY PROCEDURE by accelerator pedal can be repeated a limitless number of times; The RECOVERY PROCEDURE by accelerator pedal must be carried out fully (5 digits); there will be no message if one or more digits of the entered code are incorrect; the only way to check whether the code is correct is to complete the procedure and try to start the engine; the procedure can nevertheless be interrupted by KEY OFF. If the accelerator pedal is released before a time-out (8 s the first time, 4 secs the other times), the EOBD warning light will not go out and the RECOVERY PROCEDURE will be aborted. To start the recovery procedure, the user must carry out the following operations in order: Read the code on the CODE CARD. Turn the key to ON. The diagnosis warning light comes on for the self-test; Press and hold down the accelerator pedal. The diagnosis warning light goes out after 8 s. When the diagnosis light goes out, release the accelerator pedal. After the pedal has been released, the warning light will flash at a frequency of 0.8 Hz duty cycle 25% ON. When the warning light has come on a number of times equal to the first digit in the code, press and hold down the accelerator pedal to allot the NCM to recognise it. The diagnosis light will come on and stay on, fixed, for 4 s. When the diagnosis light goes out, release the accelerator pedal. After the pedal has been released, the warning light will flash at a frequency of 0.8 Hz duty cycle 25% ON. When the warning light has come on a number of times equal to the next digit in the code, press and hold down the accelerator pedal to allot the NCM to recognise it. The diagnosis light will come on and stay on, fixed, for 4 s. When the diagnosis light goes out, release the accelerator pedal. Repeat operations 7 and 8 for the next digits up until the last. After the pedal has been released, when the last digit has been recognised, the warning light will flash at a frequency of 1.6 Hz duty cycle 25% for 4 s, or will go out sooner, if engine starting is recognised (>450 rpm) indicating that the code has been accepted, or will come on fixed to indicate that the code has been rejected. If the code is accepted, start the engine. If the code is rejected, repeat the procedure from point 2. For NCMs which measure time, engine starting is permitted within 10 minutes without repeating the procedure. The above diagram shows an example of entering a code (which is 42173). SPECIFICATIONS: The alarm system carries out: perimeter surveillance volumetric surveillance surveillance against tilting of the car (with tilt sensor) surveillance of cutting the supply cables surveillance on the ignition key block. The system is coordinated by the BC which sends/receives commands from the external modules via the serial line: The system is switched on/off via the remote control interfaced with a received located in the BCN; the remote control and receiver are at radio frequency. The alarm system is also switched off by inserting an enabled key recognised by the ALFA CODE (emergency switching off). When it is switched on, the doors are locked. When the system is switched on, volumetric protection can be excluded. After an attempted break-in, a blinking code emitted by the dissuasion warning light indicates which sensor has detected it: this warning light also indicates the state of charge of the transmitter's battery. DIRECT INPUTS: Negative signal from switch indicating driver's door open (NO) Negative signal from switch indicating passenger's front door open (NO) Negative signal from switch indicating rear left door open (NO) Negative signal from switch indicated rear right door open (NO) Negative signal from switch indicating switch open (NO) Negative signal from switch indicating bonnet open (NC) +15 Serial line with Volumetric Sensors Control Unit (VSCU) Radiofrequency receiver DIRECT OUTPUTS: Serial line with Siren Control Unit (SCU) Serial line with Volumetric Sensors Control Unit (VSCU) Operation of front right direction indicator Operation of rear right direction indicator Operation of right side repeater Operation of front left direction indicator Operation of left side repeater Operation of rear left direction indicator Operation of hazard warning lights LED A-Bus serial line COMPOSITION STRUCTURE The alarm system consists of the following modules: Body Computer: manages the system's functions and controls the external modules. Sensors on doors, bonnet, boot: detect attempts to open the doors, boot, bonnet. Remote control system (transmitter + receiver included in the BCN). Stand-alone siren: emits beeps and the acoustic signal. Ultrasound sensors: detect movements inside the interior compartment. Anti-tilt sensor: detects a change in the car's tilt following lifting. A-Bus serial line: connects all the modules relating to the alarm system. 1 - BCN 2 - Door switches 3 - Siren 4 - Ultrasound sensors 5 - Key OPERATION There are eight states in which the alarm system may be: DISABLED; REST; ON; SURVEILLANCE; ALARM; OFF; PROGRAMMING; DIAGNOSIS. Each of these states is described in the following paragraphs. OFF The OFF state is the state in which the BC is whenever an enabled key is recognised by the ALFA CODE. This operation automatically switches off the alarm. In the OFF state, the alarm system does not respond to the receiver's commands.(key on ON) From the OFF state, you move to the rest state by turning the key to KEY-OFF. REST The rest state is the base state of the alarm system. From this state, you can change to the state of: diagnosis: when a diagnosis session is activated by a diagnostic instrument connected to the BC. surveillance: when, by means of a command to switch on and passing through the switching on stage, the car is to be protected OFF: when an enabled key is recognised by the immobilizer. In the rest condition, the BC continues to acquire the state of +15 to prevent the change to surveillance and, above all, to alarm. This information distinguishes the two basic modes of the rest state: car operating (+15 present), or abandoned (+15 absent), which is a prelude to the surveillance condidtion. EXCLUSION OF VOLUMETRIC SENSORS Volumetric protection can be excluded manually in the rest state. Exclusion of volumetric protection automatically switches off the volumetric sensors, which interrupt the emission of ultrasound. Exclusion is activated by the ignition key by means of a consecutive sequence, in strict order, of KEY-OFF (<2 s), KEY-ON (<1s), KEY-OFF, starting from a STABLE KEY-ON state: at the end of the manoeuvre, the dissuasion warning light comes on for 2 s to indicate that exclusion has taken place. If, at the end of the sequence, the reoccurrence of the +15 signal lasts less than 30 s (for example to shut windows accidentally left open), the exclusion continues to remain active. The re-enablement of the volumetric protection must take place if the occurrence of the +15 lasts over 30 s and at all events after the next switching off of the alarm system. 1 - Key-OFF 2 - Key-ON SWITCHING ON The switching on operation allows the alarm to change from rest to surveillance. This operation is always inhibited if the +15 signal is present. The command to switch on is effected by pressing the transmitter button, and is indicated by the direction indicators coming on for 2.5 s and by the emission of a synchronous beep. On receipt of the command, the BC activates within 100 ms the procedure for switching on the alarm, as described: Indication of switching on in progress Activation of blinkers fixed for 2.5 s Command for flashing of dissuasion light at 4 Hz Sending of BEEP command to siren System diagnosis/check The control unit carries out the diagnosis of the components: volumetric sensors module; anti-tilt module (if present); siren; Check via appropriate commands the state of the sensors: after max. of 3 seconds the siren; after max. of 4 seconds the volumetric sensors module; after max. of 4 seconds the anti-tilt module (if present). if the responses to the check commands do not arrive within the times indicated, the module in question is declared to be malfunctioning. Also check on plausibility of status of door switches (2 or 4), bonnet and boot (perimeter protection): if the non-closure of one of the entry points is detected, this entry point is excluded from surveillance. Check on door locking status: 4 seconds after switching on, the door locking status is checked and any cases of repulsion (door locking manoeuvre not carried out correctly) are recognised. Display of diagnostic information Problems present at switching on are indicated by: issue of an attenuation beep by the siren (ref. B in figure) flashing of the blinkers for siren fault (ref. A in figure) indication of type of problem by dissuasion light (ref. C in figure) Flashing at 8 Hz for 2.5 s indicates that one or more of the following causes of fault have been detected: one or more doors open boot open bonnet open door locking not done (repulsion) faulty volumetric sensors The warning light staying on fixed for 10 seconds indicates that one or more of the following causes of fault have been detected: siren faulty anti-tilt sensor faulty; if the faults are simultaneous, the priority of the indication is as described in the above point Switching on sensors Sending command to volumetric sensors module Sending command to anti-tilt module (if present) Switching on siren If the siren is working properly, the command to switch on the siren is sent and management of the heart-beat begins on the serial line. End of procedure The alarm system is switched on: the dissuasion light is operated, flashing at 0.8 Hz. Operating diagrams for blinking (A), acoustic signal (B) and dissuasion LED (C). 1 - Switching on of blinkers 2 - Siren fault 3 - Fixed light INTERRUPTION BECAUSE OF SWITCH-OFF REQUEST If, during the switching-on stage, a switch-off command is received from the remote control, the procedure is interrupted and the switch-off phase is entered. If visual or acoustic indications are in progress, these are interrupted to give way to the switch-off indications. SECRET CODE FOR SWITCHING ON SIREN At the time of switching on, the BC generates a random code which it sends to the siren with the switch-on command. The siren memorises the random code. When the switching off of the alarm system is requested, the BC sends the switch-off command to the siren together with the random code: the siren compares the code with its memorised code and is only switched off if the comparison is positive. In this way the system is protected from intrusion attempts aimed at deactivating the siren. In addition at each switch-on the BC memorises in EEPROM: code used any excluded external modules condition of entry points (doors, boot), so as to have this information available even after an undesired reset of the system AUTO SWITCH-ON The auto switch-on operation allows the alarm system to change from rest to surveillance automatically and on a timed basis. There are two methods of auto switch-on. FROM KEY-OFF KEY-OFF is detected The auto switch-on counter starts counting If a transition from open to closed on any of the doors or the bonnet or boot is detected, the counter restarts from zero. The counter reaches the 'AUTO SWITCH-ON TIME' The BC checks whether an enabled key is inserted If an enabled key is inserted, auto switch-on is carried out If an enabled key is not present, auto switch-on is carried out PASSIVE method KEY-OFF is detected The auto switch-on counter starts counting If a transition from open to closed on the driver's door, or any of the doors or the bonnet or boot is detected, the counter restarts from zero if the counter reaches the value of 2 minutes without any transition from open to closed being made, auto switch-on is cancelled. the counter reaches the 'AUTO SWITCH-ON TIME' the BC checks whether an enabled key is inserted if an enabled key is inserted, auto switch-on is carried out if an enabled key is not present, aut switch-on is carried out The auto switch-on methods are enabled depending on the operating modes (see country map table 'PASSIVE AUTO SWITCH-ON ENABLEMENT' and 'KEY-OFF AUTO SWITCH-ON ENABLEMENT'). Surveillance from auto switch-on is complete for all entry points; the operating modes make it possible to: activate/deactivate volumetric surveillance activate/deactive the anti-tilt module In auto switch-on, the system test is carried out as in ordinary switch-on. Door locking is not activated during auto switch-on. The visual/acoustic indications are enabled by the operating modes The definition of the driver's door in the different versions (right-hand drive and left-hand drive) is specified during end-of-line programming by the manufacturer. RE-SWITCHING ON Re-switching on allows the alarm system to change ffrom rest to surveillance automatically when, after an authorised switch-off, there are no door/bonnet/boot openings or other consistent actions. The re-switching on procedure is as follows: The alarm system is switched off The re-switching on counter starts counting If a transition from closed to open on any of the doors, or the bonnet or boot is detected, re-switching on is cancelled. The counter reaches the 'AUTO SWITCH-ON TIME' The alarm is switched on taking account of any exclusions of parts of the system (volumetric protection, siren, etc.) carried out at the last switch-on. SURVEILLANCE During the surveillance state, the BC carries out the following operations: Check +15 signal The BC acquires information on the presence of the +15: if it detects the presence of the +15 signal for over 100 ms without a previous switch-off command, the BC interprets this manoeuvre as a theft attempt and issues the command for the change to the alarm state; Exclusion of external modules because of low battery voltage If the battery voltage remains 8.5 V for over 30 minutes, the BC switches off the external modules (volumetric sensors, anti-tilt sensor, external input modules) in order to protect the battery's life and the possibility of subsequent engine starting. Perimeter surveillance The BC checks the state of the six inputs coming from the four doors, bonnet and boot: if one of these changes state for over 100 ms, the BC changes to the alarm state. Management of heart-beat command During surveillance, the BC periodically sends a command to the siren, in order to check the condition of the serial connection between the two devices: this periodical command is called 'heart-beat' and allows any attempts at intrusion or cable cutting to be detected on the serial line. Every 500 ms, the BC sends the heart-beat command via a crypto-rolling code to the siren and checks that it has been received correctly. If the BC does not manage to send the heart-beat command, the crypto-rolling code is updated as follows: the BC does not manage to send the command (e.g. because of a short-circuit on the serial line): the BC makes 2 further attempts to send the command without changing the crypto-rolling code. the BC sends the command but the serial line is disturbed: the BC makes 2 further attempts to send the command without changing the crypto-rolling code. the BC sends the command but the state of the siren is not correct or there is a loss of synchronisation on the heart-beat signal: the BC makes 2 further attempts to send the command, changing the crypto-rolling code at each attempt. If after the attempts to repeat the command, the heart-beat synchronisation is not restored correctly, the BC changes to the alarm state and implements the necessary counter-measures (activation of blinkers, etc.). As the siren also no longer receives the heart-beat command, the blinkers visual indication will be accompanied by the acoustic indication activated by the siren, which will intervene at the same time as the BC (for 3 failed attempts at heart-beat exchange made every 500 ms). At all events, the heart-beat command continues to be issued until the system is switched off, and also during the alarm state. Protection from false alarms due to reset of the bc During the surveillance stage, it is possible that an external disturbance or attempted break-in causes a reset of the BC which re-initialises its functions. In this case, the BC checks whether the alarm was on before the reset, so as to be able to re-synchronise the heart-beat with the siren, avoiding a false alarm. The BC also switches on the external modules again, except those excluded at the last switch-on. In the case of a reset, there is no visual/acoustic indication to the outside. Activation of alarm During the surveillance stage, the alarm may be activated, not only by the perimeter protection, but also by the external modules (ultrasound, anti-tilt, etc.) or the siren (because of cut cables). On receipt of one of the alarm activation signals, the BC immediately changes to the alarm state, triggering the cycles determined for the type of alarm received. Anti-intrusion strategy If, during the surveillance stage, the BC reads on the serial line a siren switch-off command, or an ultrasound switch-off command or an anti-tilt switch-off command, interprets this situation as an attempted intrusion into the system, in order to exclude the acoustic alarm or the car's protections. On receipt of one of three commands, the BC changes immediately to the alarm state, triggering the cycles determined in the case of alarm caused by cut leads. ALARMS If one of the surveillance sensors identifies a faulty situation (attempted or successful intrusion, interference and/or theft of the vehicle), the alarm system changes to the alarm state. The alarm state is characterised by the actuation of visual/acoustic indications consisting of the activation of the siren and direction indicators. Indications The indication consists of a succession of 'alarm cycles'. The parameters relating to the operating modes are defined in the 'operating modes' table. The BC is responsible for managing the type, number and duration of the alarm cycles in accordance with the operating mode: the siren may actually be activated (start of acoustic emission) and deactivated (interruption of acoustic emission). For example, if the operating mode involves the emission of 3 alarm cycles lasting 26 s with 6 s pauses, the BC will behave as follows: Activation of blinkers and activation command to the siren with relevant sound configuration parameters. After 26 s deactivation of blinkers and deactivation command to the siren 6 s wait. Repetition of points 1, 2 and 3 until the end of the required cycles. Memorisation of the cause of alarm For diagnostic purposes, a record is kept of the causes of alarm recognised by the BC. The BC memorises in a table the last 10 causes of alarm, associating with each of the causes the state of the alarm system at the time of switching on the system. The following causes of alarm can be memorised (alarm caused by ...): left front door right front door left rear door right rear door ultrasound sensor anti-tilt sensor (if present) cutting of siren cables boot bonnet +15 cut cables +30 intrusion on the siren with incorrect siren switch-off command intrusion on the external modules with command to switch off ultrasound or anti-tilt incorrect heart-beat For each cause of alarm, the state of the system is memorised, described by: left front door open right front door open left rear door open right rear door open ultrasound sensor faulty faulty anti-tilt sensor (if present) faulty siren serial line not working From the alarm situation, you change to the following states: rest: with a switch-off command or by recognition of an enabled key by the immobilizer at Key On. surveillance: at the end of activated alarm cycles DEACTIVATION Deactivation may take place either in the surveillance state, or in the alarm state. It is carried out by pressing the button on the transmitter, which instructs the BC to deactivate the alarm system in accordance with the following procedure: deactivation is indicated by two flashes of the blinkers at 1Hz ± 10%, d.c. 50% and two beeps (the indication is enabled/disabled depending on the operating mode). This indication is activated within 100 ms from receipt of the deactivation command: the siren is deactivated. the external modules are deactivated. the BC interrupts perimter protection and all counter-measures in progress, if there are any. The command is also accepted in the presence of the +15 signal. After carrying out deactivation and at the first Key-On, the control unit indicates discharged transmitter batteries, alarms from volumetric, anti-tilt, perimeter sensors,+15 and +30. The indication takes place by the flashing of the dissuasion light for 120 ± 10% s. The meanings of the flashing are as follows: Light on fixed: transmitter batteries discharged (disguises all the indications) 1 flash one or more doors 2 flashes boot 3 flashes bonnet 4 flashes ultrasound module 5 flashes anti-tilt module 6 flashes +15 7 flashes +30/earth 8 flashes serial line (no signal/incorrect signal from siren for more than 3 times) 9 flashes at least three causes of alarm The flashes last 0.5 s ON, 0.5 s OFF and the indications are repeated after a pause of 1.5 s. If there are two different causes of alarm, these are displayed in cycles. PROGRAMMING OPERATING MODES The programming state allows the BC to memorise in EEPROM the active operating mode. The operating mode can be changed by diagnostic instrument or the following manual procedure: set the ignition key to Key-On; activate the hazard warning flasher press the rear fog light control button and hold it down using the ignition key, carry out the following sequence in strict order: Key-Off (for less than 2 s), Key-On (for less than 1 s), Key-Off, starting from the Key-On state, always holding down the rear fog light button. at the end of the sequence, the siren emits 5 beeps to indicate the activation of programming. release the rear fog light switch and press it again the same number of times as the desired mode (each press gives a feedback beep) If the button is pressed for an invalid number of times (e.g. greater than the number of available operating modes), the siren emits 5 beeps and is cancelled and the country code is not changed: set the ignition key to the Key-On position within 10 s of the last press on the rear fog light button. the siren emits the same number of beeps as the number which indicates the selected operating mode: each beep lasts 1 s and is followed by a 0.5 s pause. at the end of the beeps, set the key to the Key-Off position: the BC is programmed in the new operating mode. Cancelling the procedure If, during entry of the operating mode, the rear fog lights button is not pressed within an interval of 10 s, the procedure is aborted: in this case the siren emits 5 beeps to warn the operator and the BC maintains the previous operating mode. The market can be changed from 1,2,3,4,5 using the diagnostic instrument or manual procedure. It is not possible to enable/disable the market by setting the value 0 DIAGNOSIS OF EXTERNAL MODULES The BC conducts a diagnosis on the serial line connecting to the siren and external modules, checking whether there is a short circuit to earth or to the battery or an open circuit. The diagnostic check on the serial line is carried out at the time when the communication is activated, typically when the alarm system is switched on. The diagnosis on the external modules is carried out when the system is switched on, by means of the diagnostic commands from which the following information is obtained: There are no diagnostic checks on the perimetral protection switches. Siren: not working (sound transducer faulty) already on (misalignment between BC and siren) does not respond (communication with siren not possible - serial line broken) Ultrasound module: not working does not respond (communication with module not possible - serial line broken) Anti-tilt module (if present): not working out of range (fitted incorrectly) does not respond (communication with module not possible - serial line broken) The diagnostic information obtained at the time of switching on is memorised in EEPROM to ensure that system repairs can be carried out. To carry out diagnosis, use the diagnostic equipment supplied. ACTIVE DIAGNOSIS During a diagnosis session, the BC may be asked to carry out a diagnostic check on the external modules: the BC then sends the appropriate command and communicates the result to the diagnostic instrument. If, during this operation, the BC does not manage to communicate with the module, the response to the diagnostic instrument will be: interference on serial line module does not respond Similarly a diagnostic check on the serial line may be requested, which may have the following results: OK, short circuit to earth, short circuit to battery. It is also possible to read the table relating to the alarm causes memorised in the BC. RECOVERY If an external module (ultrasound, anti-tilt etc.) is recognised as working, it is excluded for the whole surveillance cycle. When the system is switched on again, the diagnostic check is repeated on the modules which have to be reactivated if recognised as working. Composition The remote control system comprises: transmitter: is built into the key handle, it is on radio frequency and sends a variable code to the receiver. It has two or three function control keys and an LED for checking the transmission of the code and the state of charge of the batteries. receiver: radiofrequency built into the NBC with operating frequency of 433.92 MHz. Each transmission generates a variable code, managed by a mathematical algorithm. Transmitter The following figure shows the transmitter. 1 - Lock button 2 - Unlock button 3 - Boot button Specifications: The transmitter is the device which transmits the command code to the receiver; it is built into the key handle Composition The transmitter has a radio frequency stage at 433.92 MHz with range of 20 m. It has 3 buttons and one LED: the buttons activate the control, while the LED visually checks that the transmitter is sending the code and indicates the discharged battery condition. Pressing the buttons can be perceived by the user to allow tactile control of the command received. The position of the buttons is such as to prevent or minimise the risk of involuntary activations (e.g. at the time of key-on). Button operation The remote control has 3 buttons called lock, unlock, boot. LOCK: when the lock button is pressed, the doors are locked. When the button is held down for more than 4 s, the windows are closed and the sunroof is closed (SUPER LOCKING). When the button is released, the movements are interrupted; to resume movement press again for 4 seconds. UNLOCK: when the unlock button is pressed, the doors are unlocked and the courtesy light is switched on. If the button is held down for more than 4 s, the windows and sunroof are opened (SUPER OPENING). When the button is released, the movements are interrupted; to resume movement press again for 4 seconds. BOOT: When the button is pressed, the boot / tailgate is released, visible by it lifting slightly. Receiver Specifications: The receiver is located in the BCN and has a wire aerial which emerges from the body computer. Composition Receiver module with operating frequency 433.92 MHz, and has the following functions: it receives and decodes the signals coming from the transmitter it manages the memorisation of a maximum of 8 transmitters it generates the command for opening and closing the doors (actuating as appropriate the exit from blinker command, if required). it activates and deactivates the alarm system. it generates the command to light up the timed courtesy light. Operation The remote control and receiver system has two operating states: switch on; switch off. Switch on command With the switch-on command, the receiver sends a signal to the BCN which: activates the door locking issues the instruction to change from rest to surveillance to the larm system, in the case of prepared BC. The command to switch on is made by pressing the button on the transmitter: it is indicated by the direction indicators coming on for 2.5 s (the indication is enabled/disabled by EEPROM). Switching on is always inhibited (except in diagnosis) if the key-on +15 signal is present. While the button is being pressed, the flashing frequency of the transmitter LED is 3 Hz. The transmitter makes a complete transmission of the variable code in response to continued pressure on the button lasting at least 50 ms. If the button is held pressed continuously, the transmitter interrupts the transmission after 20 s; to transmit further, release and press again the button on the transmitter. If the receiver recognizes a continuous transmission (code received always the same), after the initial switching of state, it excludes the possibility of a continuous switching of the control. SWITCHING ON The receiver acquires the variable code, compares it with the codes memorised during programming and recognises it as one of those. After recognising the code, the receiver controls the locking of the doors and the change from rest to surveillance of the alarm in the case of prepared BC. In the case of BC with alarm system, if the car has already been locked with the mechanical key, when the transmitter button is activated the BC should activate the door locking/alarm switch-on as follows: Doors locked with key and alarm switched off (auto switch-on time not yet elapsed): no door locking or switching on of the alarm Doors locked with key and alarm switched on (auto switch-on time already elapsed): operation of door locking (opening) and switching off of alarm. Doors unlocked and alarm switched off (auto switch-on time not yet elapsed): operation of door locking (locking) and switching on of alarm. Doors unlocked and alarm switched on (auto switch-on time already elapsed): no operation of door locking and switching off of alarm. The activation of the blinkers indicates the change of state of the door locking in accordance with the figure: A - Locking command B - Locking command with repulsion C - Unlock command Comfort function The comfort function (function present in BCN on request) is obtained by pressing the transmitter button for less than 4 s; after receiving the signal, the receiver transmits a suitable command to the BCN which interprets it as: command to activate the controlled window closing/opening Boot opening function When the boot opening button is opened, the boot may be opened, and the receiver, after recognising the message from the remote control, sends the message to the BCN for: boot unlock switching off of anti-theft protection Deactivation After receiving the switch-off command from the transmitter, the receiver sends a message to te BCN which: instructs the unlocking of the doors permits the change from surveillance/alarm at rest in the case of prepared BC. Switching off is carried out by pressing the button on the transmitter: this is indicated by two flashes of the blinkers at a frequency of 1 Hz, d.c. 50%, (function enabled/disabled by EEPROM). Switching off is also enabled in the presence of the +15 signal. The receiver controls unlocking following the same rules as those described in the switching-on section (obviously only if the lock status is active). The alarm system is also switched off. Transmitter batteries run down information With the switch-off command, the receiver sends the alarm system the batteries discharged status. The transmitter indicates the batteries discharged condition by issuing, when activated, a single flash lasting 200 ms when the button is pressed: the transmitter returns to the normal flashing mode if the battery charge returns to above the pre-established threshold. From the moment the transmitter signals the batteries discharged condition, 100 switch-on / switch-off actuations are guaranteed. The correct indication of the battery status is restored at the 2nd activation of the transmitter after the batteries have been replaced. PROGRAMMING Specifications: The receiver/transmitter system is programmed at the end of the line together with the ALFA CODE. During the car's life, the receiver can be made to learn new transmitters, for example in the case of new keys or cancellation of lost keys. At each new programming procedure, all transmitters not presented during the above-mentioned procedure are eliminated from memory. At each programming, all the available transmitters must be programmed. The transmitters not presented are deleted from memory. Key programming procedure The remote control key programming procedure is managed by the diagnostic equipment and can only be activated by entering the CODE'S ELECTRONIC CODE. The procedure is divided into 2 parts: key learning (during which the secret codes of the keys are received by the BC) and a memorisation (during which the codes received are memorised permanently in the BC's EEPROM memory). Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to initialise the key learning procedure and gives confirmation to the operator. the operator presses the button on the key to be memorised holding the button down, the operator requests learning: the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to learn the remote control key. the BC receives the secret code and the ID of the key and learns it. the diagnostic instrument confirms completed learning and the operator releases the button. the previous steps are repeated for each remote control key which has to be learned, up to a maximum of 8 keys. once all the keys have been learned, the operator asks the diagnostic instrument to memorise the keys. the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to memorise the keys learnt: only the keys learnt during the procedure will be memorised in EEPROM (so all the keys currently memorised are lost and each key not learnt during the procedure will not be memorised). Blinker enablement/disablement Using the diagnostic instrument, blinker enablement/disablement is possible in order to adapt the vehicle to the market where it is sold.

GLOSSARY AF (ALTERNATIVE FREQUENCY): Radio function which makes it possible, whilst receiving an RDS programme broadcast by several transmitters on different frequencies, to automatically switch to the frequency with the best reception. BALANCE Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the sound distribution between the left and right side speakers. BASS Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the acoustics (LOW TONES) EON Radio device function which makes it possible to receive information on traffic conditions from radio channels not currently tuned into, temporarily interrupting the station being listened to. FADER Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the distribution of the sound between the speakers FM Long wave radio transmission frequency between 8705 and 108 MHz. GPS (GLOBAL POSITIONING SISTEM) Satellite location system, whose purpose is to provide any user the possibility of deciding his position on the earth's surface. GSM Communication standard for mobile equipment (GSM= Global System for Mobile Communcation) currently used in about 90 countries, enjoying optimum coverage. LOUDNESS Radio function which makes it possible to improve the sound by increasing the low tones. LW Long wave radio transmission frequency between 153 and 279 kHz. MW Long wave radio transmission frequency between 531 and 1602 kHz. CONNECT Info Telematic Node POI (Point of interest) Consists of typing in a sequence of information in order to select a particular point of interest (in relation to which information can be obtained) PTY Radio function which makes it possible, with the RADIO mode activated, to select the type of programme, e.g. NEWS (news and current affairs), AFFAIRS (politics and events), etc. for the radio stations which provide this type of information. normal status, with all the functions activated or able to be activated; stand-by, with the functions partly activated and the screen dark System activation The system is activated automatically when the ignition is turned ON and it assumes the status activated before it was switched off last time (normal or stand-by). When the ignition key is turned OFF or removed, the system comes on by pressing the left knob (T16) or the SOS button (T22) for a 'Service Call' (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the telephone). Turning the system off The system switches off automatically when the ignition key is turned to the OFF position. The conditions and functions activated before the system is switched off are memorized and will be restored the next time it is switched on. The switching off is delayed if a phonecall or an emergency call is in progress or if there is a change of language for the voice instructions by about 20 minutes after the call has ended or at the end of the function. If the system has been switched on using the knob (T16) or the button (T22) with the ignition key in the OFF position or extracted, it is switched off by pressing the knob (T16) again or it switches off automatically about 20 minutes later to preserve the battery. Stand-by (dark) Whilst the system is operating with the ignition key inserted, it can be placed in the stand-by mode by pressing the MAIN button (T17) at length. This operating condition (Dark) corresponds to a dark screen with the volume off, but the system continues to work invisibly and therefore the telephone is ready to receive calls. If the limit of an activated function is exceeded in the stand-by mode, a warning is displayed. To return to normal operating conditions, press the MAIN button (T17) or the emergency call button (T22) briefly (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the phone). Volume adjustment To increase the volume: turn knob (T16) clockwise To reduce the volume: turn knob (T16) anticlockwise During adjustment, volume level is shown graphically on the display (this type of display is present only on the main menu for the radio source). The volume of the PTY31 Alarm/Traffic Announcement (TA), phone, phone ringer and voice recognition may be adjusted separately. Automatic volume reset during phone calls During phone calls, the radio volume is reset automatically and the display shows the phone symbol. Mute function (audio volume reset) Hold key (T18) down to deactivate volume of the audio system (Radio, CD, CDC) with any operating mode active (MAIN, NAV, TRIP); the radio thus goes off and the message 'Audio OFF' appears on the display Give key (T18) a short press to turn the radio back on. This reactivates the audio function with the relevant screen. Nav mute function (exclusion of navigation system voice messages) Hold the NAV key down to deactivate the navigation system voice instructions (T20). The volume gradually decreases (Soft Mute function) and the message 'NAV MUTE' appears on the display. Give the NAV key (T20) a long press to deactivate the NAV MUTE function: the volume will gradually increase (Soft Mute function) to the previous setting. With the NAV MUTE function active, all other navigation system functions can be used and the MUTE function will be ignored if traffic information is received with the TA function active or an emergency alarm is received. Soft mute function When the MUTE function (audio system) or NAV MUTE (navigation system) is turned on or off, the volume falls or rises gradually (Soft Mute function). The Soft Mute function is activated when one of the six preselection keys numbered 1 to 6 , key (T13) or key (T15) is pressed to tune the radio stations. Anti-theft protection The CONNECT system has an anti-theft protection system based on the exchange of information with the electronic control unit (Body Computer) which prevents it from being used on another vehicle even if it is equipped with a Body Computer. The protection system means that the telematic system cannot be used once it has been extracted from the dashboard and stolen. This 'recognition' procedure is carried out each time the engine is started. This system guarantees maximum security and prevents the secret code having to be entered each time after the radio supply is disconnected (for example when the battery is disconnected). Each time it is reconnected an automatic test procedure is conducted; if the result of the test is positive, the system starts to work, whilst if the codes compared are not the same, the display shows a message on the display which asks the user to enter the 4 digit secret code Entering the secret code The four digit secret code, represented by black asterisks, should be entered using the telephone keypad and confirmed by pressing the knob (R2). The figures entered are shown by red asterisks which replace the black ones. If one of the code digits needs correcting, press the ESC button (T24) briefly to cancel it, then enter the correct digit. Pressing the ESC button (T24) for longer cancels the entire secret code entered. After entering and confirming the secret code, a message appears on the display advising the user that the recognition procedure is in progress. If the outcome of the test is positive, the system starts to work normally, whilst if it is not, the screen for entering the code appears again. The system will not work until the correct code has been entered. The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system. Personal data If the system fails, it cannot be repaired. Instead the full system must be replaced and this entails the loss of any personal data in the memory. Thermal protection This complex strategy makes use of several sensors. The following functions are disabled/enabled according to passenger compartment interior temperature: up to 75ºC the system works normally, from 75ºC to 85ºC, the volume is limited, the CD player (audio and maps) is disabled and the phone works normally, at 85ºC the phone is disabled, at 90ºC the system is completely disabled. The user must wait for passenger compartment temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated. Y. Functions A. Functions active B. Volume reduction from 75° C, audio/map CD deactivated from 75° C, phone deactivated from 85° C C. Self-deactivation Protection against overheating The telematic system components come with an overheating protection function that cuts off operation when the relevant module temperature exceeds a set limit. In this case, the function activated by the module that has reached the temperature limit is deactivated and a message for the user appears on the display. The user must wait for the module temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated. Conversely, to exit from the message screen immediately and activate a different function, press the ESC key (T24). The can network The TIN is a+15 node connected to the B-CAN network; this means that at Key OFF, the CONNECT is not connected to the network and cannot be reactivated by the network. The Key On signal is in fact a direct signal to TIN. Navigation system (nav) General information The satellite navigation system is activated by pressing the NAV key (T20) which gives access to the main functions. 1 Screen display active 2 Screen layout display 2 Display of pictogram information The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions (pictograms/maps) and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers. The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the left and right milometers, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'. This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base. The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel. The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information. The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle. GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed. If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated. The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck). If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data. The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects. This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed. The system constantly compares the information coming from the wheel sensor, the GPS aerial and the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way. The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed. If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading. During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete. The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map. Internal functions (localisation) The GPS measurements used inside the CONNECT nagivation system are: 1 - Estimated position of the vehicle expressed as Latitude / Longitude Latitude/Longitude values refer to the satellite and are expressed as radiants and Height in metres. The Latitude indicates the reference parallel. Parallel zero is the equator. Car position is therefore defined as the meridian arc between the point of the car and the reference parallel. It is essential to indicate whether the latitude is North or South, i.e. it is necessary to specify the hemisphere within which the car is located: North or South, the maximum value is 90°. The longitude indicates the reference meridian. The zero meridian passes through Greenwich (near London). The car's position is therefore defined as a parallel arc between the car's point and the reference meridian. It is essential to indicate whether the longitude is East or West, the maximum value is 180°. 2 - Vehicle's speed in m/s along the south-north / east-west axes. 3 - PDOP of the GPS point (in actual fact an estimate of the variance on the GPS position error). 4 - Quality data relating to the signal received: (number of satellites, South/North relationship, point in 3D). 5 - Time-fix relating to the last measurement made (makes it possible to identify to which instant the measurement refers). The following message is displayed on the screen: 'The Alfa Romeo navigation system guides you through the traffic and helps you reach your destination. The highway code in each country must be respected. These take priority over the manoevres indicated by the navigation system. The driver has sole responsibility for driving the car and observing the highway code.'. Screen elements and functions The main informations and functions supplied and managed by the navigation system are as follows: acoustic and visual instructions with indication of distance from destination and estimated time of arrival; Detailed maps in different colours with different scales, two and three-dimenstional perspective, to show the position of the vehicle, the route and the destination clearly; Personalization of the navigation system with the possibility of entering pre-memorized destinations with the name of the road and street number; Automatic storing of the last 8 destinations; Name of the road currently being driven along; Possibility of selecting the route according to one's preferences; Information on current position; Information on journey time; Fault diagnosis of the sysem and warnings about possible problems. If the system contains an incorrect CD-ROM or an audio CD or no CD ihas been inserted, the display invites you to enter a CD whenever the system required a navigation CD-ROM to compute the route or update a map. Navigation functions are managed mainly using the knob: turn the knob to magnify the map to different levels; press the knob to call up the first menu page on the screen; access later menu pages by selecting the 'Other menu' option and confirming using the knob; the menu page disappears when the knob is pressed again. Graphic instructions The manoeuvres to be carried out are displayed on the main navigation function page and the MAIN page (T17) by means of arrows and symbols. The arrow at the bottom represents the next manoeuvre (turn left, turn right, turn around, go straight on or reverse direction) while the arrow or symbol at the top represents the one after that. The number shown under the arrow indicates the car's distance from the turning. The small arrow low down on the right of the display (on the MAIN page) or in the top box (on the main page of the navigation function) indicates the destination direction. The estimated time of arrival and the distance left to travel are also indicated near this arrow. Audible instructions The audible instructions guide you to the destination recommending the manoeuvres to be made and, in particular, the manoeuvre is announced first and then detailed instructions are given. It is possible to have these instructions repeated by pressing the RPT button. Navigation cd-rom drive The navigation system CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the telecoms system and is also used for the audio CD. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation system drive simultaneously. The navigation system can, however, operate partially even without the navigation system CD-ROM inserted. In this case, when the key is pressed to expel the CD-ROM with the navigation function activated (so an audio CD can be inserted), one of two things may happen: the system cannot currently compute the required route; the route computed before the navigation system CD-ROM was extracted is still valid. In the first case, the car position alone will be displayed and you will be asked to insert the navigation system CD-ROM. In the second case, the system is able to provide instructions to the destination and asks the user if the guide is to be maintained or not. If the user selects and confirms NO, the system continues as in the first case. If YES is selected, the system stores the relevant part of the map; this operation takes a few instants and the display asks the user to wait. When the CD-ROM is loaded, it is ejected and the system resumes the navigation system function with the maximum scale of '2 km'; in this case, not all the route may be visible. Under these conditions, navigation is limited and and certain functions and commands will not be available. The information shown in the map will also be restricted. When the navigation system is no longer able to continue guiding the driver to the destination, or the car leaves the portion of the map that has been loaded, the display asks the user to load the navigation system CD-ROM. If the user does not insert the CD-ROM the system operates as described in the first case above, i.e. suspending the map information and continuing using GPS information (car location and number of satellites available). When the new CD-ROM is inserted, the system software will automatically be updated with the new maps or new functions. During the operation, a message will be displayed asking the user to wait and at the end the destination memory will be empty. When the 'From reset' function is set, the on-board computer provides information relating to the last manual zeroing of the computer. With the 'B from hh:mm' function, the information is determined starting from the last manual zeroing of the computer or automatically from the last time the engine was switched off (ignition key turned to the OFF position) separated from the next starting by a period of at least two hours. The data stored on the on board computer (average speed, distance travelled and journey time) are reset manually using commands on the instrument panel display (see User Handbook). This information also appears on the display (for about 4 seconds) whenever knob (R2) is turned. The parameters of both functions are always available so that the user can move from one to another The following information is available: Instantaneous consumption Average fuel consumption Range Average speed Journey distance Journey time Distance to the destination Arrival time The distance from the destination and the arrival time are available with the navigation system activated. The system stops indicating residual range for values lower than 15 km (dashes are shown instead of the range value in km). In the case of refilling with the fuel warning light on, the system onlyupdates the remaining range figure if, when the refilling takes place, the quantity of fuel in the tank is above about 1/4 of the capacity (18 litres). For lower refuelling values, the range value prior to the refuelling continues to be indicated. 'instant consumption' Indicates vehicle fuel consumption while driving and is therefore useful for showing fuel consumption for the driving style adopted. This value is the same as the two on-board computer functions ('From reset' and 'B da hh:mm'). The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres. 'average fuel consumption' Indicates average fuel consumption measured since last refuelling. The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres 'range' Indicates the distance in kilometres the car still has to travel before it will need refuelling. The calculated journey range depends on the amount of fuel still present in the tank and the average fuel consumption. 'average speed' Indicates average car speed calculated from the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer. The value is expressed in 'km/h' (kilometres per hour). 'journey distance' Indicates distance in kilometres travelled by the car since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer The value is expressed in 'km' (kilometres). 'journey time' Indicates time since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer. The value is expressed in '(h) (m)' (hours and minutes). 'distance to destination' This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates distance (in kilometres) between current car position and the set destination. 'arrival time' This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates the estimated time at which the set destination will be reached. The time is indicated in 'hh:mm' (hours and minutes). The indicated arrival time is obtained by increasing the remaining journey time by some 30%, calculated on the basis of average speed added to current time.
