The assistance call menu comprises the following functions: Infomobility (*) Medical assistance ((*) Roadside rescue (*) Personal number Emergency 112 Settings (*) Functions requiring subscription to Targa Services 'infomobility' When the 'Infomobility' function is selected and confirmed using knob (R2), a message is sent to the service provider with an information request. When the provider receives the message, it activates a phone link. When the link is active, the user may ask to forward the information request to the operator. If the telecoms link with the service provider cannot be activated, a warning message appears on the display. The telecoms system attempts to reconnect to the service provider information service in any case. Some information will be sent directly by the operator while other information will be sent via SMS messages that are received regardless of which function is active (MAIN, AUDIO, etc.). The message appears directly above the screen active at the time, inside a window that contains functions 'Save', 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call'. If the 'Save' option is selected, the message will be stored, while if 'Delete' is selected, it will be eliminated from the display and from memory. If 'Map' is selected, the point on the geographical map will be displayed automatically, with the possibility of inserting it as the destination of the navigation system. In this case the message will also be stored automatically. If 'Call' is selected, the telephone number contained in the message will be dialled automatically and the message will be stored. If a message sequence is received, a special window will be opened for each one and it will be possible to carryout the save, delete, display on map or call telephone number operations. All message received will be saved unless they are deleted. The list with all the messages is visible at the bottom of the display, in the main screen of the 'Infomobility' function. Each message is identified by an icon indicating type, date and time sent. To access individual messages in the list, which may contain traffic information, points of interest or weather information, activate the 'Select' function using knob (R2), then turn to scroll through the list of messages (including the part that cannot be seen). When the message you want to read is highlighted, press knob (R2) to display on the screen. An icon with a 'T' identifies messages with traffic information (e.g. accidents). When the message contains geographical information to help locate the point, the options 'Delete' and 'Map' are made available when the display appears. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays the map that shows the position of the point of interest from the event. An icon with an 'i' identifies messages with information on points of interest or general information. When the message is displayed, the 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call' options are available. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays a map that shows the position of the point of interest that may also be used as destination or inserted in the system list. With the 'Call' button, when present, a call can be sent directly to the number indicated in the message. The icon with an 'i' also identifies messages with general information (weather conditions, atmospheric events, etc.). When one of these messages, not accompanied by geographical information for location, is displayed, only the 'Delete' option is available, which allows it to be removed from the list permanently. 'medical services' When this function is selected and activated, a medical assistance request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the Targa Services operator. The message is forwarded after a waiting time of 10 seconds. When Automatic medical assistance is activated by means of the 'Settings' function (described below), the message is sent when the CONNECT key (T22) is pressed with no further need to select a specific function. To prevent accidental call-outs, when Automatic medical assistance is selected, the user is allowed a time of 15 seconds after pressing the key by accident to stop it. All you have to do it turn knob (R2) to another option. The number of the medical assistance centre cannot be set by the user. 'roadside assistance' When this function is selected and activated, after 10 seconds a roadside rescue request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the Targa Services operator. The number of the roadside rescue centre cannot be set by the user. For both Roadside Rescue and Medical Assistance requests, if the telecom transmission is not successful, the freephone number for the required service will be dialled automatically, to report the need for assistance (the telephone call will only be successful if there is GSM coverage of the area where the car is). 'personal number' When this function is selected and activated, a phone call is automatically forwarded to a number set previously by the user. The setting of this number is described under the next function 'Settings'. 'emergency 112' When this function is selected and activated, a call is sent out directly to the public emergency services. '112' is the emergency services number for all countries where this public service is available. A 112 emergency call can always be made even if there is no card in place. 'settings' When this function is selected and activated, a new screen is accessed which proposes the display of the CONNECT CODE (code identifying the system terminal), memorisation of the 'Personal number' and configuration of the type of 'Medical Assistance', as described above. The phone number entered in the space corresponding to 'Personal no.' identifies the user who will be called in an emergency. Selecting the type of forwarding used for 'Medical Assistance' calls activates or deactivates the automatic transmission of the medical assistance request message when the button is pressed (T22). When the call has been sent, the display shows a 'call sent' message for 4 seconds. If the assistance call cannot be forward for any reason, the display shows a notification message, asking you to press knob (R2) to go back to the main screen. If a phone call arrives after activating the assistance call function, the notification will not be shown on the display but the ringing will be heard. If the user decides to accept the call and presses the phone key (T1) briefly, the assistance call screen disappears. If the user rejects the call with a long press on the phone key (T1), the assistance call continues. Turning the system off There are two different ways of switching the CONNECT system off: switching off independent of the ignition key switching off dependent on the ignition key To make this choice, access the SETUP menu. Antitheft protection The CONNECT is protected against theft and unauthorized systems by means of an 'authentication procedure'. This type of check involves other devices installed on the vehicle including the Body Computer which uses messages exchanged via the telematic network and is activated each time the system is switched on. The procedure is not activated if the CONNECT system is switched on using the knob (R1) or the button (T22) and if the ignition key is in the OFF position. In this case the CONNECT system works normally without carrying out the authentication procedure. Entering the secret code If the ignition is switched ON, the user is asked to enter the 4 digit Master Code to allow access to the standard functions. The Master Code is unique to each CONNECT system and cannot be deleted. To enter the code, a special screen must be accessed. After having entered the code, a second screen indicates that the authetication procedure is in progress. If the correct code has been provided the system is fully enabled; conversely, if an incorrect code has been entered, the screen is cancelled and the previous screen with the words 'The code entered is incorrect' appears. Enter the master code or switch the system off using the ON button. There is no limit to the number of incorrect codes that can be entered. The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system. Voice controls The user can use the voice recognition function to control the CONNECT by voice in order to carry out certain phone functions. There are two different methods for the voice activation function: with voice identification; without voice identification. In the first case the system is capable of recognizing the command by comparing the voice command with a sample memorized previously. In the second case the system is capable of receiving voice commands irrespective of the voice. Voice recognition and message storage operations are immediately interrupted by an incoming call; In this case, the entire operation must be repeated at the end of the call. The arrival of SMS text messages does not interrupt operations. Voice messages This function allows the user to record and replay six voice messages, in order, with a total maximum duration of 30 seconds for each message. If the memory is full, the oldest message is overwritten. When the time available elapses, the operation ends automatically. The recording activated by the user can last for a maximum of 30 seconds, and is terminated automatically at the end of this available time. However, the user can interrupt it manually. Both the beginning of the recording and the end (either terminated by the user or because the memory has run out), are identified by an appropriate acoustic message (double beep). The Voice Memo allows you to listen to voice messages from the last message recorded and then all previous messages. Once the buffer is full, the messages are played again from the first (in a continuous loop). The Voice Memo allows the entire buffer available for recording to be deleted. Navigation system (nav) General information The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers. The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the milometer, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'. This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base. The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel. The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information. The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle. GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed. If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated. The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck). If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data. The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects. This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed. The system constantly compares the information coming from the milometer, from the reversing sensor, from the GPS aerial and from the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way. The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed. If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading. During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete. The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map. Navigation cd-rom drive The navigation system CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the telecoms system and is also used for the audio CD. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation system drive simultaneously. The navigation system can, however, operate partially even without the navigation system CD-ROM inserted. In this case, when the key is pressed to expel the CD-ROM with the navigation function activated (so an audio CD can be inserted), one of two things may happen: the system cannot currently compute the required route; the route computed before the navigation system CD-ROM was extracted is still valid. In the first case, the car position alone will be displayed and you will be asked to insert the navigation system CD-ROM. In the second case, the system is able to provide instructions to the destination and asks the user if the guide is to be maintained or not. If the user selects and confirms NO, the system continues as in the first case. If YES is selected, the system stores the relevant part of the map; this operation takes a few instants and the display asks the user to wait. When the CD-ROM is loaded, it is ejected and the system resumes the navigation system function with the maximum scale of '2 km'; in this case, not all the route may be visible. Under these conditions, navigation is limited and and certain functions and commands will not be available. The information shown in the map will also be restricted. When the navigation system is no longer able to continue guiding the driver to the destination, or the car leaves the portion of the map that has been loaded, the display asks the user to load the navigation system CD-ROM. If the user does not insert the CD-ROM the system operates as described in the first case above, i.e. suspending the map information and continuing using GPS information (car location and number of satellites available). When the new CD-ROM is inserted, the system software will automatically be updated with the new maps or new functions. During the operation, a message will be displayed asking the user to wait and at the end the destination memory will be empty. If a route is activated when the RG is deactivated, it remains visible on the map whilst the new automatic recalculation of the route is not activated. VOLUME: this allows the adjustment of the volume. HOME1/HOME2: this starts the calculation of a route towards one of the two pre-set of habitually used destinations. INFO: this shows information on the GPS position and the route set. DETOUR: this allows the activation of an alternative route. SETTING OF ROUTE: this defines the parameters for calculating the route and allows the activation of the junction zoom. DESTINATION AND ROUTE: this manages the destination and allows the activation of the calculation of the route. VOICE AGENDA: this manages the voice navigation agenda. The message is forwarded after a waiting time of 10 seconds. When Automatic medical assistance is activated by means of the 'Settings' function (described below), the message is sent when the CONNECT key (T22) is pressed with no further need to select a specific function. To prevent accidental call-outs, when Automatic medical assistance is selected, the user is allowed a time of 15 seconds after pressing the key by accident to stop it. All you have to do it turn knob (R2) to another option. The number of the medical assistance centre cannot be set by the user. 'roadside assistance' When this function is selected and activated, after 10 seconds a roadside rescue request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the 'TARGASYS' operator. The number of the roadside rescue centre cannot be set by the user. For both Roadside Rescue and Medical Assistance requests, if the telecom transmission is not successful, the freephone number for the required service will be dialled automatically, to report the need for assistance (the telephone call will only be successful if there is GSM coverage of the area where the car is). 'personal number' When this function is selected and activated, a phone call is automatically forwarded to a number set previously by the user. The setting of this number is described under the next function 'Settings'. 'emergency 112' When this function is selected and activated, a call is sent out directly to the public emergency services. '112' is the emergency services number in all countries where this service is available. A 112 emergency call can always be made even if there is no card in place. OPERATING PROBLEMS The CONNECT system is capable of detecting and solving both any faults that are produced inside the system and any overheating problems OPERATING FAULTS: if an internal fault relating to a certain module (audio, telephone, etc.) is identified, the system 'freezes' the last available screen and launches a diagnostic search. The system checks the module involved for a certain length of time to determine the type of fault; if the fault persists when this preset time is exceeded, the best action to solve the problem is implemented (e.g. resetting the hardware for the module involved). If the system no longer responds to the commands, it can be restarted manually by pressing the TRIP button (T21) 4 times in the space of 3 seconds. PROBLEMS DUE TO OVERHEATING: if the temperature of one of the system hardware modules (audio, telephone, CD player, etc) exceeds the maximum limit, the module will signal that it is overheated; a dedicated warning message will appear on the display. The module concerned will be automatically restricted or disabled. In extreme cases the entire system is automatically shut down until the temperature returns to normal and this will be shown on the display, as illustrated in the diagram. To exit the dialogue window, press the 'ESC' button; the module involved will operate on a restricted basis: Overheating of the 'Audio' module: if the 'Audio' module overheats, the sound volume is automatically restricted irrespective of the audio source activated (radio, CD, CD Changer). A special warning message for the user will appear on the display. Overheatin of the 'CD Player' module: if the 'CD Player' module overheats, no type of CD can be read: no audio CD can be listened to and the navigation functions cannot be guaranteed (unless the navigationsystem was activated previously without a CD). A warning message for the user will appear on the display. Overheating of the 'Telephone' module: if the 'Telephone' module overheats, the module will be deactivated (TEL OFF) with the inhibitaion of the information and service functions (SOS). A special message for the user will appear on the display. System auto-switching off; in the case of extreme overheating, a warning will notify the user that the system auto shut down procedure has begun. When normal temperature operating conditions are resumed, the user can switch the system back on again. Anticrush sensors on driver and passenger side window seals These take the form of an electrical circuit in a sheath applied to the driver and passenger side upper seal. The control unit (NPG) interface contains two analogue inputs (signal and earth) with A/D (i.e. conversion from analogue to digital signal) for the microcontroller. Roughly-speaking, these sensors are made up of a resistor with a value of 400 to 1800 ohms under normal conditions, i.e. when the glass does not compress the seal. The NPG downloads information about the presence or absence of an obstacle when the window is closed (raised) via the anticrush seals. Under these conditions, the resistance signal reaching the control unit must be between 0 and 400 ohms during manual or automatic operation. As a consequence of this event, the control unit must immediately suspend window travel and immediately (max. 30 ms) reverse it for 400 ms. Special software strategies are naturally also preset to handle changes in the electrical properties of the sensors due to wear, ageing etc. With key ON. If the anticrush protection cuts in on three consecutive occasions within 1 minute, the NPG must allow the relevant window to be raised in steps (max. consecutive 200 ms of control) until the upper stop is reached (window closed - managed by current control). When the stop is reached, all error conditions are reset under the following conditions: upper stop reached; upon a K-OFF, K-ON operation once the window has been lowered for at least 400 ms. Climate control strategies In order to achieve a comfortable, satisfactory climate within the passenger compartment as quickly as possible, the system must be able to determine the outdoor environmental conditions and engine temperature at the time the system is activated. In other words, if the system is activated at a time when the outdoor temperature is very low and the engine is cold, it must behave differently from other situations such as: outdoor temperature low and engine warm or, conversely, outdoor temperature high and engine cold. In order to implement the ideal operating strategy, the system must thus consider the outdoor temperature level at the time the vehicle is about to set off (i.e. when the key is turned ON) and also with the vehicle in motion, when the outdoor temperature read by the sensor could experience changes. The system thus acts as follows; when the ignition key is turned from OFF to ON, the system electronic control unit detects blended air temperature: If blended air temperature is lower than 40 ° C, the system stores the outdoor air temperature value that the sensor is measuring. If blended air temperature is higher than 40 ° C, the system considers the outdoor temperature value stored before the key is turned OFF. This occurs because, since the engine is warm, the system considers that the vehicle has stopped for a short time and environmental conditions are as before the halt. The outdoor temperature value is again updated while the vehicle is in motion because the outdoor temperature sensor could be influenced under these conditions by temperature changes in the moving outside air. The system then uses a speed signal from the CAN network. The signal is considered in relation to a threshold value of 0-30 km/h: If car speed does not exceed 30 km/h, the outdoor air temperature value is updated only if it is lower than the value stored previously when the key was turned ON. If car speed exceds 30 km/h for at least 1 minute, the outdoor temperature value replaces the previously stored value, whether it is lower or higher. Supplementary functions of driver's door node (npg) with options fitted The driver's door node (NPG) enables the following functions only with options packages fitted: front window closure from recirculation control; front window closure from pollution sensor; front window closure from remote control. Window closure from recirculation control The function is active with the ignition key ON, provided the electric window system is fitted with efficient anticrush seals. Briefly, when the driver's door node (NPG) receives recirculation status information from the climate control system (NCL) node via the CAN network, it controls activation of the electric window actuators. The control is implemented in sequence at 50 ms intervals in the following order: passenger window; driver's window Closing wndows from pollution sensor The function is active with the ignition key ON. The climate control system software is designed to activate recirculation mode if the air to be taken in to the vehicle passenger compartment is polluted. The climate control system node (NCL) sends a signal via the CAN network to indicate that recirculation is activated to the driver's door node (NPG) , which activates the front window central locking. Closing windows from remote control unit Because the body computer node (NBC) is responsible for managing central closure (AUTO CLOSE) and opening (AUTO OPEN) of the doors, it can also manage opening/closure of the front windows (as well as the electric sunroof and courtesy lights) where this function is available. The remote control unit is equipped with three buttons marked lock, unlock, boot and takes the form of a sending unit built into the key grip. It is fitted with a radio stage (433.92 Mhz) with a range of 20 m. When a button is pressed, a variable code controlled by a mathematical algorithm (rolling code) is sent to a receiver built into the body computer (NBC). This node comes with a wire aerial that emerges and runs into the facia wiring (the aerial plugs into the facia wiring harness by means of a connector and can therefore be changed). The function is active with the ignition key off, provided the window system is equipped with an efficient anticrush seal. Door closure lock operation (autoclose) 1 long blink When the lock button is pressed (single, short press) all the doors are locked and the alarm (if present) is activated. Unlocking the doors using the remote control and not opening the flaps, the Body Computer commands the closing of the doors after 2 minutes. Door opening release operation (auto open) double short blink When the release button is pressed (single short press), all doors are released and the alarm (if present) is deactivated; The courtesy lights also come on for 15 seconds or until key on. DOOR AND BOOT OPENING INDICATOR This function is active with the key ON. Negative signals (earth) from the door open switches (front and rear wheel, and boot) combine to activate a warning light on the control panel (NQS). In practice, when one or more lines from the above switches are earthed for longer than 50 ms., the body computer that controls the status of these inputs downloads the status and relays it to the CAN network in this case, the instrument panel (NQS) is responsible for processing the information and controlling the warning light DOOR OPEN MICROSWITCH One is present for each door; these are actually the inputs from the control unit (NBC) used also by the door open check, courtesy light and alarm. If one is closed to earth (door open), the doors cannot be locked. REPULSION FUNCTION The lock and release motor control relays are located on the body computer printed circuit (NBC); Action time is 700 ms ± 10%. At the end of this period, the body checks switch position: if they do not tally it emits a repulsion command. The repulsion function takes place following a lock manoeuvre or after a release manoeuvre. In practice, when the motors are controlled to lock and the operation is not carried out correctly (i.e. the controls do not tally), the body orders an opposite manoeuvre in an attempt to realign the catch microswitch contacts. INHIBITION DUE TO A HIGH NUMBER OF MANOEUVRES If 10 or 11 individual open/close manoeuvres are carried out within 25 seconds, the circuit inhibits the door lock/release function for a further 30 s. The last manoevre before inhibition is always a release. After an inhibition period of 30 seconds, the circuit becomes operational if the bar commands are consistent. If the switches are not aligned, the circuit need not carry out any manoeuvres. The switches must be moved once inhibition is complete in order to carry out manoeuvres. BATTERY FLAT If battery voltage is low, and - within 20 ms of the onset of door lock/release manoeuvres - battery voltage (power supply) drops below a threshold of 9V, the device must suspend operation and enter inhibition mode for 30 s. When supply voltage prior to actuation is already lower than 8 V, commands must be ignored. PROTECTION Protection is required for the motors alone in the case of relay binding. No protection is required against motor short circuit to Vbatt and earth because this is provided by the relevant fuse If the fault persists (relay binding), the NBC does not implement any catch lock/release controls and informs the user of the fault. If one of the two connections remains connected to Vbatt (relay with blocked contacts), the microprocessor must activate the other relay to restore the connections to the same potential and deactivate the motor current. The active relay coil continues to use power and can unfortunately drain the battery.

SPECIFCATIONS The rear doors have been designed with the structure and the panels not featuring any corners to reduce the risk of injury to the occupants. The arrangement of the exterior opening handle is particularly innovative as it is fully integrated in the rear door pillar. The locks and control levers are protected against break ins by a shield which prevents access to the mechanisms from the outside. The side panel features: an armrest which contains the controls for the electric windows and the opening/closing handle; interior door opening lever; two speakers, one of which is housed in the door opening lever trim; The sliding glass is made from thermal glass and is moved by means of a mechanism with a guided cable. The system is available, on request, with an anti-crush safety device, housed in the upper seal, which stops the ascent of the window if there is an obstacle in between as the window is closing. The trim on the upper profile of the door, by the glass, and the glass scraper trims, ensure a perfect seal and the absence of aerodynamic wind noise. COMPOSITION The luggage compartment node (NVB) is located under the rear seat and manages and operation of the rear electric windows. OPERATION The Luggage Compartment Node carries out the following functions: supports the functions described in the table; receives and sends information on the B-CAN line (e.g. diagnosis, commands) connects with the rear wiring. Procedure for communication of subfunctions carried out by nodes is: C= via CAN; D = direct communication. View of connectors. A - E09LA 18 way B - E09LB 8 way Pin-out CONNECTOR A CONNECTOR B Electric rear windows The NVB control unit controls the operation of the left and right rear electric window motors which can operated both manually and automatically: the closing of the rear windows can only be activated manually, whilst they can be opened either manually or automatically. Manual system Mode is manual when the user starts and stops the system by hand by means of the control buttons. The motor stops when the buttons are released. Automatic system Mode is automatic when movement is started by pressing the control button for a period in excess of a preset value. In automatic mode, window arrest (electric power to window motor cut off) is brought about by: the window reaching the upper or lower end of its travel the safety system (anticrush) once a new raise or lower control has been pressed. This is regulated by controlling motor current, which must be self-adaptive, and by managing the anticrush sensor. In the case in question: the control unit does not operate when the buttons are pressed for less than 60 ms. manual movement is activated if the control key is pressed for between 60 ms and 300 ms (short control); automatic operation is activated if the control button is pressed for longer than 300 ms (long control) Key on Movement takes place as described in the table Key off Movement is only manual and timed by the NBC, which controls service relay 2 supplying the NPG and NVB nodes. Note that service relay 2 is located on the facia control unit (CPL) - T13 - is active with the ignition key ON and deactivated temporarily during start-up. If an INT signal is not received from the ignition, the NBC maintains service relay 2 supplying the windows and sun roof active and changes the timing for 3 minutes ± 10% but deactivates it immediately when one of the two front doors is opened. If a window control (front or rear) is pressed within three minutes of controlling service relay 2, the NBC resets the timer for a further 3 minutes. Control buttons There are two control buttons on the rear doors; but the buttons located on the driver's front door can also be used, as described below. Each time the window function control buttons are pressed, the buzzer in the NQS goes off as confirmation: this information is supplied via the CAN: it is then the task of the NQS to manage the duration and tone and when to activate the signal if there are simultaneous commands. Disablement Glass movement is disabled by: Vbatt = 16 V (re-enabled for Vbatt = 15.5 V) Vbatt = 10 V (re-enabled for Vbatt = 10.5 V) The battery voltage level is supplied to the network by means of a specific message. Safety sensors in rear door seals These take the form of an electrical circuit in a sheath applied to the glass upper seal. The interface for the NVB control unit involves two inputs (signal and earth) from the sensors which are made up of a resistor with a value of 400 to 1800 ohms under normal conditions, i.e. when the glass does not compress the seal. The NVB downloads information about the presence or absence of an obstacle when the window is closed (raised): in these conditions, the resistive signal is between 0 and 400 ohm. As a consequence of this event, the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the glass and reverses it. Special software strategies are naturally also preset to handle changes in the electrical properties of the sensors due to wear, ageing etc. Rear electric windows diagram Wiring diagram 1 - Body computer node (NBC) 2 - Facia control unit (CPL) 3 - Driver's door node (NPC) 4 - Luggage Compartment Node (NVB) 5 - Left rear door electric windows control 6 - Right rear door electric windows control 7 - Left safety sensor seal 8 - Right safety sensor seal 9 - Left rear electric window motor 10 - Right rear electric window motor Electric rear windows go ahead and control from driving seat Electric rear windows control. The rear windows (on 5 door versions only) may be controlled by the NPG once this mode has been selected using the 'REAR' button. If the button is pressed, the NVB function is activated and the rear windows can be moved by operating the window switches on the NPG. If no movement is made, the selection returns automatically to the front windows 20 minutes after the last window movement (NPG). Each time the rear windows are operated, the rear window selection maintenance time is reset. To make a visual check, when the rear windows are selected, a LED is activated which stays on throughout the selection on the NVB. If the front part of the button is pressed, the NPG function is operated and the front windows can be moved by operating the window switches on the NPG. The function may be activated only if rear window inhibition status is not present. Inhibition of rear window control from driver's side The rear controls can be inhibited (protection) via a 'LOCK' rear movement button. The NPG downloads this switch and indicates the inhibition by means of an LED in the back of the switch and makes the status available to the network. The NVB does not allow the rear windows to be moved and turns off the control key lighting. Luggage compartment node (nvb) additional functions The NVB control unit enables the following functions only with options packages fitted: rear window closure from recirculation control; rear window closure from pollution sensor; rear window closure from remote control. Window closure from recirculation control The function is active with the ignition key ON, provided the electric window system is fitted with efficient anticrush seals. To sum up, when the NVB receives 'recirculation status' information from the climate control node NCL via the CAN, it controls the activation of the electric window actuators. Closing wndows from pollution sensor The function is active with the ignition key ON. The climate control system software is designed to activate recirculation mode if the air to be taken in to the vehicle passenger compartment is polluted. The climate control system node NCL sends a signal via the CAN to indicate that the recirculation is activated and the NVB activates the electric window actuators. Closing windows from remote control unit Because the body computer node (NBC) is responsible for managing central closure (AUTO CLOSE) and opening (AUTO OPEN) of the doors, it can also manage opening/closure of the windows (as well as the electric sunroof and courtesy lights) where this function is available. The remote control unit is equipped with three buttons marked lock, unlock, boot and takes the form of a sending unit built into the key grip. It is fitted with a radio stage (433.92 Mhz) with a range of 20 m. When a button is pressed, a variable code controlled by a mathematical algorithm (rolling code) is sent to a receiver built into the body computer (NBC). The function is active with the ignition key off, provided the window system is equipped with an efficient anticrush seal.

SPECIFICATIONS The tailgate is manufactured using conventional pressing processes and includes large window bonded flush with the tailgate. The edges that overlap the structure are screen-printed in black. The window features a demisting circuit that also includes the area around the third brake light and the rear wiper blade parking area. The tail-gate can be opened: by turning the key directly in the lock; by using the button in the centre of the dashboard; by remote control, via a button on the ignition key. The tail-gate is held in position by two gas struts. SPECIFICATIONS The car features two compartment lids, i.e. the bonnet lid and the fuel filler flap. The bonnet lid consists of an exterior trim assembled on a support frame. Strips of sealant are applied between the trim and the frame. These limit vibrations while also increasing overall rigidity. The fuel filler flap is made out of plastic in the same shade as the body and is moved by hand. A press-fastener is fitted to hold the flap in closed position BONNET LID The bonnet lid, made through traditional pressing processes, is fitted with a frame with pre-established collapse lines. This safety feature, together with specific retaining hooks, prevents the lid from penetrating the windscreen in the case of an impact. The bonnet is lined throughout with a preformed panel in sound-absorbent material. This reduces noise emissions to the outside of the car and also to the car interior to increase passenger comfort. To lower aerodynamic noise still further, the front and rear sides of the engine bay are fitted with two seals. Moulded foam blocks are also fitted behind the two hinges. The panel is fastened to the frame by means of press-studs and is made out of compressed textile fibres coated with oil and water-repellent material that is preformed by hot-pressing. The pressing process includes the perimeter finish and holes for fastening. The lid is supported by two hinges, each fitted with a fastening hook made out of the moving part of the hinge. The lid is opened and closed by a single central catch that incorporates a safety hook The catch is opened by a bowden cable operated by a lever located in the lower side area of the facia on the driver's side. View of bonnet lid components 1 - Bonnet lid 2 - Lid hinge 3 - Retaining hook 4 - Telescopic struts 5 - Wind seals 6 - Bonnet catch 7 - Soundproofing trim FUEL FILLER FLAP View of fuel filler flap 1 - Fuel filler flap 2 - Retaining nuts 3 - Pin 4 - Flexible flap retaining seat The fuel filler flap is made out of plastic in the same shade as the body and can be operated manually from outside. The flap hinge mount is secured by two nuts accessible from inside the wheel arch. A pin on the inside of the flap fits into a flexible seat to hold the flap closed.

SUNROOF All vehicles can be fitted as an option with an electrically-operated sun-roof which can , on some versions, also be operated by a remote control. The sun-roof is adjustable by means of a selector to nine positions in addition to the closed position. This allows the air flow around the passenger compartment to be optimised. To ensure safety during movement, the sun-roof is fitted with an anticrush safety device that cuts out movement in the presence of obstacles. SPECIFICATIONS: The sun-roof unit is made with a sliding part made out of tinted glass. This is operated electrically by means of an electric motor and can be adjusted to nine positions over and above closed position by means of a selector (three tilted positions to form a spoiler and six concealed sliding positions). A sealing strip around the edge of the sun-roof is in contact with the roof profile. The sun-roof is also fitted with a rigid, hand-operated blind that shields the light. The selector is located on a courtesy light between two ultrasound sensors and controls the electric operating motor by means of a control unit. The sun-roof is moved by two flexible racks to which are anchored the guides that pull the expanding pullies that support the sun-roof. To limit possible damage to passengers or objects caused by the roof when in movement, an anticrush function is active during roof closure, when the panel is sliding and also during tilt manoeuvres. Drainage channels on the front and rear of the frame drain off water that could filter from the seals through pipes with antireflux valves if the roof is not completely closed or misaligned. COMPOSITION The figure shows the sun-roof components 1 - Tinted glass 2 - Seal 3 - Sun blind 4 - Drainage pipe 5 - Drainage channel 6 - Deflector 7 - Mechanical guide 8 - Motor 9 - Potentiometer 10 - Flexible racks 11 - Extending support mechanism 12 - Mechanism guard The system consists of: an electric displacement motor with Hall-effect position and speed sensors a sliding frame with a flexible rack pulling system; an electronic control unit built into the electric motor assembly; a selector with inhibition control, used to move the sun-roof to different positions. OPERATION The sun-roof is moved along the slide guides on the frame by means of an electric motor. This may be controlled manually by a selector or remotely (on certain versions) by means of a command sent by the Body Computer (DF5505) to the control unit. The motor moves flexible pulling racks housed in seats on the frame. These are anchored to extending mechanisms that suport the sun-roof, which is moved to the required point or position. The sun-roof is equipped with an underlying blind that can be slid along by hand by means of a handle. This is designed to keep out sunlight. When the sun-roof is fully opened and concealed, the blind is pulled completely inside the roof panel. When the sun-roof is closed, the blind emerges partially so that it can be more easily grasped. The sun-roof may be moved manually by means of the selector under the following conditions: with key on; - the roof can be moved remotely, i.e. when the control unit receives control signals from the Body Computer (DF5505), under the following conditions: opening/closure by means of the remote control, with a central window locking system fitted and after locking the doors, by depressing the remote control button for longer than 10 seconds, i.e. the time required for a full travel - (function active with key-off); In remote control mode, the sun-roof opens or closes automatically whatever the selector position. Automatic closure can be interrupted at any time by pressing the selector upward (inhibition position) or altering selector position (it is locked in this case). A new command can be given after 10 sec. by means of the remote control or - with key-on - by means of the manual selector). During movement, slide/tilt operations (including operations controlled remotely), the anticrush protection is always active do not disconnect the battery or supply the sun-roof with power during motion. If this happens, the control unit loses its memory and must be reset as described in the relevant paragraph. ANTIPINCH FUNCTION To limit possible damage to passengers or objects by the moving roof, an anticrush function is active during closure, when the panel is sliding and when the roof is tilted. If effort in excess of a given threshold is detected, the control unit interprets this as an obstacle and stops movement immediately before moving the roof back by about 10 cm if it is sliding - or in the fully open position if it is tilting. The anticrush protection can be cut out by setting the selector to the inhibition position as follows: select the required position; press the selector down vertically and hold down during movement until the selected position is achieved. Selector View of manual control selector 0 - Roof closed position B1- Minimum tilt position B3 - Maximum tilt position S1 - Minimum slide position S6 - Maximum slide position The manual control selector is adjustable: by turning the knob anticlockwise to three preset tilted spoiler heights from B1 to B3; by turning the knob clockwise to six preset concealed sliding positions from S1 to S6; to position 0 corresponding to roof closed. This position can be identified because it is stiffer to click into; on inhibition position (all selector connections earthed) by pressing the selector down vertically. Control unit Sun-roof movement is controlled by an electronic control unit housed in the casing integral with the motor. The unit processes signals from the selector or remote control via the body computer and also controls the anticrush protection function. The function is controlled by the control unit, which receives position and speed information from Hall effect sensors fitted to the motor. When effort in excess of a certain threshold is detected, corresponding to a higher current uptake, this is interpreted as an obstacle. The control unit then stops the roof immediately and moves it back in the opposite direction by about 10 cm. The control unit also receives a vehicle speed signal because the vacuum created at certain speeds could change the effort required to close the roof and under certain conditions this could be interpreted as an impediment. The control unit therefore uses this signal to ensure movement is not halted inadvertantly. Emergency manoeuvre View of activation points for emergency movement. 1 - Volumetric sensor mount 2 - Electric control motor 3 - Operating key If the electric movement device fails to operate, the sun-roof may be moved manually as described below: prise up the volumetric sensor mount; fit the 4 mm socket wrench provided into the seat on the motor; turn the wrench clockwise to open the roof or anticlockwise to close it. Alignment Procedure for alignment on the car If repairs require both sun-roof and motor to be removed at the same time and then refitted, if you are not sure that the sliding guide position has been maintained, restore alignment between the two guides before the parts are refitted because sun-roof alignment is no longer guaranteed and water and air may enter. To restore guide alignment, proceed as follows with the motor disconnected: move the extending support guides by hand until they are fully opened on both sides and ensure that sliding has completed; move the support levers into (roof closed) position; align the through holes on the pulling guides with the blind holes on the support levers by means of two pins (one on each side) 3mm in diameter as shown in the following figure; View of guide alignment procedure. 1 - Support lever 2 - Pulling guide A - Reference pin introduction point Proceed as follows to align the guides: hold the pins in position and refit the motor remove the alignment pins; reconnect the motor to the electrical system and the selector to the control unit; refit the sun-roof to the extending mounts and adjust the position to ensure correct alignment and a perfect seal. carry out the control unit memory resetting procedure as described i the relevant paragraph; renew the guide shield trims. Procedure for alignment at the bench With the sun-roof assembly on the bench, following procedures that involve removal of the motor and moving or sliding parts, proceed as follows to align the sun-roof guides and position the mobile parts correctly: fit the removed parts except for the motor; move the extending support guides by hand until they are fully opened on both sides and ensure that sliding has completed; move the support levers into (roof closed) position; align the through holes on the pulling guides with the blind holes on the support levers by means of two pins (one on each side) of exact diameter as shown in the previous figure; hold the pins in position and refit the motor. Then remove the alignment pins; refit the sun-roof to the extending mounts and adjust the position to ensure correct alignment and a perfect seal. refit the sun-roof to the vehicle and reset the control unit memory as described in the relevant paragraph.

SPECIFICATIONS The fixed body windows, windscreen and rear side windows are bonded flush with the body. Together with the rear window, they help increase the structural rigidity of the body and increase the level of car safety while greatly reducing aerodynamic noise. WINDSCREEN The windscreen glass is tinted and laminated. It consists of two layers of glass with a sheet of plastic in between. This configuration prevents the glass layers from shattering if struck by stones and pebbles. This maintains visibility and above all ensures a high degree of protection if the window is struck by the head. The window border that overlaps the body is screen-printed in black The windscreen is fitted, on some versions, with a rain sensor bonded near the rear view mirror mount base and a demisting sensor located on the base itself a few millimetres away from the windscreen. REARSCREEN The rear window is made out of tempered, not laminated, glass and bonded flush with the tail-gate structure. A set of demisting rheophores on the inner surface of the rear window include the third brake light installation area and the wiper parking area. The rheophore is connected to the electrical system by means of two terminals located on the right and left sides of the rheophore. The rear window border that overlaps the tail-gate structure is screen-printed in black FIXED SIDE WINDOWS The fixed side windows are made out of tinted tempered glass and bonded flush with the body. A sealing strip on the pillar side of the windows prevents turbulence and wind noise with the door closed. The rear window border that overlaps the tail-gate structure is screen-printed in black

SPECIFICATIONS All vehicle interior trim is designed to satisfy severe international flame-resistance standards. The main components are slow-burning: they do not ignite due to accidental contact (for example, if a cigarette is dropped), flames do not develop and, in the presence of fierce heat they burn to produce strong, dense smoke. Trim design and configuration is aimed at producing a high level of acoustic comfort combined with a high degree of passive safety. All the protrusions that could harm car occupants in the case of impact have been eliminated. Symbols describing the correct use of the baby seat in the presence of a passenger air bag are shown on the inner side of the passenger side sun visor . Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system For greater comfort, light bulbs are fitted on either side of the mirrors and on the right and left sun blinds. A courtesy light is fitted in the front of the passenger compartment and another in the rear. The luggage compartment is also fitted with a courtesy light. Puddle lights are housed in the lower rear area of the door panels (for a description of courtesy light operation . Characteristic of working principle 7005M front electric windows PASSENGER COMPARTMENT COURTESY LIGHT SYSTEM Front courtesy light View of front courtesy light A - Left switch B - right switch The front seats are lit by a courtesy light unit that contains two courtesy lights and a spot lamp, each with its own control switch. The courtesy light comes on for about 3 minutes when the door is opened (provided the door is left open). After this it goes off. If the doors are closed, for a 3 minute period the light is left on for about 7 seconds and then turned off gradually so that the car can be started. When the doors are opened using a remote control, the courtesy light goes on gradually and a timer lasting about 15 seconds activates at the same time. The courtesy light goes off gradually when the doors are locked using a remote control. The light goes off in any case when the ignition key is turned to ON. The courtesy light can be set to three positions by means of switch A (left): switch in central position (1) - both courtesy lights come on when a door is opened; switch moved to the left (0) - both courtesy lights stay off; switch movd to the right (2) - both courtesy lights stay on. The courtesy light may be set to three positions by means of switch B (right) switch moved to the left (1) - left light comes on; switch moved to the right (2) - right light comes on; switch in central position (0) - both lights stay off. Before getting out of the car, ensure that both switches are in central position (0). This ensures that the courtesy lights go off automatically after a few seconds when the doors are closed Rear courtesy light View of rear courtesy light A - Switch The rear seats are lit by a courtesy light that comes on for about 3 minutes when a door is opened and then goes off gradually. When the doors are closed, the timer of about 7 seconds is activated, as for the front courtesy light, before the light goes off. When the doors are opened using a remote control, the courtesy light goes on gradually and a timer lasting about 15 seconds activates at the same time. The courtesy light goes off gradually when the doors are locked using a remote control. The light goes off in any case when the ignition key is turned to ON. The courtesy light can be set to three positions: switch in central position (0) - the courtesy light comes on automatically when a door is opened; switch moved to the left (1) - the courtesy light stays off; switch moved to the right (2) - the courtesy light stays off. before getting out of the car, ensure that the switch is in central position (0) to ensure the courtesy light goes off after a few seconds when the doors are closed Vanity mirror courtesy light Courtesy lights on the driver and passenger side sun visors come on when the cover is opened regardless of ignition key position. They go off automatically when the cover is closed Puddle light Puddle lights in the doors feature a two-tone lens. The lower part, which lights the ground, is white while the upper warning light part is red. The courtesy lights come on when one of the doors on both sides is opened, regardless of ignition key position. They stay on for about 3 minutes with the door open and then go off gradually. The courtesy lights go off over a 3 minute period when the door is closed. PASSENGER COMPARTMENT LIGHTING Luggage compartment courtesy light The luggage compartment is made easier to use by a courtesy light located on the right wheel arch trim. This lights up automatically when the tail-gate is opend and goes off when it is closed. The courtesy light may be kept off by depressing one of its sides Glove compartment light The facia glove compartment is fitted with an interior light. The light comes on when the flap is opened and goes off when it is closed.

SPECIFICATIONS The front seats have been designed to optimize comfort and safety and ensure maximum driving comfort, ideal lateral containment properties and lumbar support. The base structure is fastened to the seat lift unit and is made out of pressed steel with an antisubmarining ridge. This prevents the occupant from sliding under the lap part of the seat belt if the car decelerates abruptly. The squab frame is made out of a pressed steel structure that improves energy absorption in the case of rear impact. This is anchored to the seat lift unit by means of a bilateral joint. On three-door versions, the squab can be tilted by means of the release handle, which allows the seat to tilt and glide forward in a single manoeuvre. Subsquent repositioning is aided by a memory mechanism in the slide guides. This allows the seat to be restored to its initial position automatically. Squab rake may be adjusted by turning a knob on the outside near the joint. The squab supports a height-adjustable head restraint. This can be moved through a travel of about 50 mm by means of a release button located on the right side of the head restraint. The seat lift unit consists of a steel frame that includes the lift mechanism. The slide guides are secured to the lift mechanism, cushion and squab. The seat belt branch fitted with the fastening sensor is secured to the inner side of the seat lift unit Driver's seat reach may be adjusted through a travel of 230 mm along angled guides. Seat ride may be adjusted through a travel of 60 mm by means of a new type of mechanism that moves the seat in an arc (a maximum height movement corresponds to a horizontal forward movement of about 50 mm). This mechanism is operated by a ratchet lever. The driver's seat squab also comes with lumbar adjustment. This is operated by means of a knob on the side facing toward the outside of the car. On certain versions, the seats are also fitted with heating pads located between the trim and padding. The heating is operated by means of a switch on the outer seat trim. On certain versions, an opening arm-rest is fitted between the seats. This is secured to the lower central trim and can be used to stow small items. SPECIFICATIONS: The rear seats are fitted with squabs built to ensure maximum occupant safety in the case of various types of impact. They also prevent items in the luggage compartment from being propelled forward. The rear cushions come with a pressed steel base with antislip profile that forms an effective antisubmarining structure in conjunction with the beam welded to the rear floor pan. The rear seat squab can be folded separately 40/60%. This feature is standard on all cars. A fold-down arm-rest is located on the squab between the two side seats. The seats are fitted with two head restraints for the side seats. these can be adjusted to two positions. Certain versions come with a third head restraint for the central seat with the same specifications. Versions with a third head restraint also come with a central inertia reel seat belt. SPECIFICATIONS: The front and rear bumpers are made out of polypropylene and contain two impact absorbing buffers. The wheel arch housings are protected by plastic semirigid plastic shields that protect the inner part of the compartment from external objects and offer partial acoustic insulation while acting as a trim element for visible parts in the wheel arch housing. The lower part of the engine compartment is protected by a cover fixed to the chassis and the bumper by bolts; in the upper section there is a series of covers which can be easily detached for maintenance operations. The other elements (grilles, badges, trims, etc.) are designed to enhance the appearance and spirit of the vehicle. COMPOSITION Absorbent buffers are fitted on all car versions: two on the front strut connection beam and two on the rear trim near the rails. The buffers are made out of expanded polypropylene. This material is resistent to temperature changes, ageing and deformation.

SPECIFICATIONS The car is fitted with seat belts with three anchorage points. As an option, the third rear passenger seat can also be fitted with a belt with automatic inertia reel. The height-adjustable front seat belts are fitted with electrically-operated pretensioners with load limiter. There is a sensor, on the branch anchoring the belt to the driver's seat which warns when the seat belt is not fastened by means of a warning light in the instrument panel (with the ignition ON). The side rear seats are fitted with seat belts with three anchorage points and inertia reel fitted to the roof panel pillars. Standard equipment for the rear seat is a lap belt with two anchorage points without reel. As an option, the car can be fitted with a seat belt with three anchorage points and inertia reel in conjunction with a third head restraint. COMPOSITION View of seat belt on car 1- Front seat belt 2 - Electrically-operated pretensioner 3 - Front belt anchorage branch 4 - Air bag control unit 5 - Side rear seat belt 6 - Inertia reel 7 - Central rear seat belt 8 - Inertia reel 9 - Rear belt anchorage branches REEL WITH PRETENSIONER AND LOAD LIMITER The front seat belt reels are fitted with electrically-activated pretensioners controlled by the air bag control unit , with a load limiting device. This device was introduced to increase passive safety and consists of a torsion bar that allows controlled yield during the restraining action in order to modulate the force acting on the shoulders. Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system REAR CENTRAL SEAT BELT REEL The rear central seat belt reel is located inside the squab anchored to the squab structure. To ensure effective operation in safe conditions, the reel is connected via a bowden cable to the squab catch release lever. The belt is free to slide and allow fastening only when the lever is properly closed. A second Bowden cable, also connected to the release lever, locks the backrest by means of a pin which prevents it folding over. The lever is used to release the backrest joint and consequently lock the reel. SPECIFICATIONS: The car is fitted with insulating panels to reduce mechanical noise and insulate the passenger compartment against noise deriving from rolling and the external environment. The luggage compartment base houses a spare wheel with tool kit. These are secured in a container which is fastened inside the rim by a device. The spare wheel is covered by a sound-absorbent preformed cover. This is turn is covered by the carpet that lines the luggage compartment floor. SPECIFICATIONS The structure of the vehicle has been designed to respond to all situations in an optimum manner guaranteeing a high level of passive safety for the driver and passengers. The parts that protrude from the car's exterior profile, with its flush-fitted windows, and the underbody have been designed with particular attention to lowering resistance of the air to the car's progress and achieving an excellent drag coefficient (Cd = 0.325) and drag coefficient by area (Cd x S = 0.667). These features lower energy consumption and noise levels due to wind noise and turbulence. SAFETY The car body is designed to crumple in controlled fashion in the case of impact from the front, side or rear, or roll-over. It absorbs impact energy without affecting passenger compartment living space by creating a survival chamber that offers effective occupant protection in the case of an accident. TORSIONAL AND FLEXURAL RIGIDITY The body's high torsional and flexural rigidity gives the car good qualities of passive strength while steering is made more precise due to correctly maintained suspension angles to generate a sensation of solidity and comfort while driving. TORSIONAL RIGIDITY DaNm / rad Unadorned body + windscreen 88600 FLEXURAL RIGIDITY DaNm / mm Unadorned body + windscreen 830 These high rigidity levels bring many advantages: lower vibrations; lower noise; – increased resistance to failure caused by the use of the vehicle over particularly uneven roads; – the sensation of a compact car; maintenance in time of the overall qualities of the vehicle. In the case of operations to the bodyshell, if the structural reinforcements are distorted they must always be replaced. RESISTANCE TO FRONTAL IMPACTS The crumple zone body is fitted with strengthening reinforcements to make the survival chamber stronger. The following main structural changes have been made to meet this requirement: floor pan reinforcements; footboard and dashboard box section reinforcements; rail reinforcements; strut reinforcements reinforcements on the dome connection beam; pillar reinforcements; suspension attachment reinforcements; addition of bonnet retaining hooks; addition of high strength facia beam in magnesium alloy 1 - Floor pan reinforcements; 2 - Rail reinforcements; 3 - Strut reinforcements; 4 - Footboard and dashboard box section reinforcments; 5 - Front pillar reinforcements; 6 - Suspension attachment reinforcements; 7 - Bonnet retaining hooks; 8 - Facia beam; 9 - Windscreen pillar reinforcements RESISTANCE TO SIDE IMPACTS AND ROLL-OVER To ensure a high safety level in the case of side impacts or roll-over, the reinforcements have been designed to limit survival chamber deformation The following main structural changes have been made to meet this requirement: reinforcements on the windscreen pillars reinforcements in the central pillars; reinforcements in the seat belt attachments; reinforcements in the lock striker attachments; beam joining central floor and front reinforcement; beam joining central pillars beneath roof panel. A further important element in resistance to side impacts consists of the doors which are described in the paragraph which follows. 1 - central pillar reinforcements 2 - reinforcements on the windscreen pillars 3 - reinforcements on the seat belt attachments; 4 - reinforcements on the lock striker attachments; 5 - beam joining central floor and front reinforcement; 6 - beam joining pillars STRUCTURE OF THE ROOF The roof structure stiffens the survival chamber assembly in the case of side impact or roll-over. The structure consists of the roof panel in addition to a central hoop, te central connetion hoop, bolted to the side pllars, and a box section hoop connecting the rear pillars. Sections of sealant are applied along the edges of the hoops in contact with the roof panel. These bond parts to confer good mechanical strength while also preventing vibrations and resonance. 1 - Roof panel 2 - Front hoop 3 - Pillar connection hoop 4 - Rear hoop STRUCTURE OF THE DOORS The structure of the doors is of fundamental importance for the safety of the passengers in the case of side impacts and has therefore been designed with optimum geometry and rigidity to keep possible injury of the occupants to a minimum. The structure of the doors includes a side impact bar, waist reinforcement and front pillar reinforcement arranged to allow them to be opened after the most severe frontal and rear impacts. An expandible sealant strip is inserted between the side impact bar and the outer door trim while a heat-moulded sound-proofing panel is bonded to the inside of the trim to damp resonances. 1 - Interior waist reinforcement 2 - Exterior waist reinforcement 3 - Pillar reinforcement 4 - Tubular side impact bar RESISTANCE TO REAR IMPACTS Side impact protection is ensured by rails and connection beams that are welded to the floor pan to create a very strong structure. This structure offers extra protection to the tank, which is secured beneath the floor pan. The rear box section trim and tail-gate ring is also a reinforced area. 1 - Left rail 2 - Right rail 3 - Connection beam 4 - Connection beams 5 - Rear box section trim 6 - Rear floor pan TYPICAL BODYSHELL MEASUREMENTS DIAGRAM FOR CHECKING UNDERBODY This chapter contains typical body measurements that may be used by bodyshops to achieve the best results if repairs are necessary. The deformations suffered by the bodyshell as the result of a reasonably severe impact almost always cause alterations to the shape and the structure of the different parts of the bodyshell. It is possible to carry out a preliminary check to assess the extent of any deformation without removing the mechanical parts. The check operation is completed by restoring the dimensions using the appropriate equipment. This procedure must always be carried out before the damaged panels are repaired and/or replaced. Remember to check mechanical elements which could have suffered deformation. MEASUREMENT POINTS ON THE VEHICLE GAP VALUES MEASUREMENT POINTS ON THE VEHICLE GAP VALUES PREVENTATIVE SAFETY SOUND INSULATION The vehicle is very quiet and the noise level at a speed of 120 km/hour in fifth gear is 70 decibels. Driving comfort (i.e. passenger compartment noise levels and roominess) has been improved mainly by insulating against road surface and mechanical noise by applying heat-expandible soundproofing materials and also taking special care over parts assembly and aerodynamics. The soundproofing materials used to lower noise level are mainly bituminous. Their role is to deaden the noise generated by mechancial vibrations from areas such as the underbody, door interior and external environment. The heat-expandible materials are synthetic rubbers or resins. Their function is to fill in boxed sections to eliminate sound propogation (wind noise). When the body is placed inside the paint-stoving ovens, these materials expand (up to ten times) and vulcanise so that they bond to the inner surfaces of panels with which they come into contact and fill the cavity. A - Sound-insulating materials B - Soundproofing materials C - Sound-deadening materials D - Heat expandible materials D - Preformed synthetic blocks The following measures have been taken to achieve an optimum level of sound insulation: insertion of heat-expandible septa in the rails, windscreen and rear window pilars, central pillars and spoilers; insertion of preformed synthetic blocks into central pillar body nodes to prevent vibrations being transmitted into the passenger compartment damping lining for panels through application of bituminous heat labile materials before painting sound-deadening linings for the front of the dashboard, the front and rear running boards, the load platform and side panels with pre-formed, composite panels sound-absorbent trim for the bonnet and roof; use of double-faced seals in the cable ducting holes between engine bay and passenger compartment; a thorough check of the sealants. All the engines and mechanical components fitted to the car belong to a new generation engineered for improved acoustic/vibrational qualities. Good aerodynamics have been ensured by improving car shape and adjusting the profiles of components that impair acoustic comfort: To maintain the high level of acoustic comfort reached, the vehicle must be restored to its factory configuration in in the case of repairs. BODYSHELL PROTECTION The bodyshell has been designed to be resistant for many years (8 years for perforation, 10 years for structural weakening) to any kind of environmental attacks as far as both the internal parts, which are not visible but potentially subject to corrosion, and the external parts, subject above all to damage which could adversely affect the appearance of the vehicle, are concerned. This result has been achieved by designing the structure of interior panels to limit exposure to corrosive infiltrations and making widesperad use of galvanised panels. Galvanising On the vehicle90% of the bodyshell consists of panels which have been galvanized, divided into 70% twin galvanized panels and 20% single galvanized. Both the outer parts and the moveable parts are made completely from double galvanized panels with the sole exception of the roof which is made from a panel which is not galvanized as it is not very subject to corrosion. Following the galvanizing treatment, the bodyshell is subjected to bonderization, a treatment which washes any grease or surface oxidation from the panels and to painting by cataphoresis, a treatment which is fundamental for protection and subsequent painting. All joints between bodyshell panels are sealed to prevent infiltrations of corrosive agents. Abrasion-proof coatings and protections Once sealants have been applied, abrasion-proof protections are added to body areas exposed to gravel chipping. This protection offers good properties of flexibility and adhesion and also makes a considerable contribution to noise damping. All opening and holes not involved in the fastening of mechanical parts are also closed. Both materials, sealants and anti-abrasives, are then dried in the oven. Areas afected by the application of sealants and vinyl protection Painting The aim of painting is to protect panels and maintain the car's appearance (gloss and richness of colour) The car colour range includes two-coat pastel shades, metallic shades and 3 iridescent shades. The type of colour for the vehicle and its characteristics are indicated on the identification plate which contains the following information:P product supplier; enamel colour and type; shade code; Type of product to be used for retouches and painting in the case of service operations. MATERIAL RECYCLING The vehicle is designed to ensure that all parts made out of plastics or elastomers (rubber) weighing more than 50 grams are marked with a coded symbol so that materials can be identified and divided during recycling. Example of marking system used on recycable parts Tables in the chapter GENERAL INFORMATION AND TECHNICAL DATA, 'Panels and body' contain symbols and descriptions of recyclable materials that can be used on the vehicle. This information is provided to help categorise materials and also to ensure that suitable products are used for internal washing, painting plastic materials, repairs, bonding, etc. during service.

Continue to Step 5 Value incorrect Eliminate blockages in the manifold Value correct Replace the brake servo/pump assembly Op. 3330D02 5 CHECKING PUMP All OK Problems met Operation Check that the brake pump has not seized Check that one or more wheels do not remain braked Continue to Step 6 Seizure of the pump Replace the brake servo/pump assembly Op. 3330D02 Seizure of a front caliper Replace the caliper Op. 3310A30 Seizure of a rear caliper Replace the caliper Op. 3310B36 The car remains braked Remove the servo/pump assembly Op. and adjust the projection of the pushrod 3330D02 The car remains braked at the rear Repair the handbrake 6 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems met Operation Test the vehicle before delivery to the customer, to check that the fault is no longer present. The driver's and passenger's electric windows only work in manual mode; when the control button is pressed for over 300 ms and released, the window does not close automatically, but instead stops. The Driver's Door Node unit is programmed to open and close the driver's window both manually and automatically, while the passenger's window can close only manually, while it can open both manually and automatically. The control unit activates the manual function if the control button is pressed for a period of between 60 and 300 ms (short time), while it actibates the automatic function if the control button is pressed for over 300 ms (long time). WARNINGS Before dIsmantling the air conditioning cooling circuit, drain the system and recover the coolant 5040A10 Air conditioning refrigerant CIRCUIT - Draining and Refilling During the operations, when the system components are disconnected, seal the connectors with suitable plugs to prevent humidity and impurities from entering the system. Before reconnecting the pipes, replace the O-rings on the connectors. Only use green coloured seals, resistant to R134A refrigerant. Lubricate the threads of the connectors with anti-freeze and tighten the connectors to the recommended torque. R134a refrigerant fluid cannot be mixed with Freon R12 used in climate control systems on previous vehicles; therefore never, under any circumstances, use Freon R12 for air conditioning systems operating on R134a. All the system components are specifically for use with R134a and are NOT INTERCHANGEABLE with those from previous vehicles using Freon R12. There is a special draining/recovery station for the R134a fluid. The anti-freeze for lubricating the compressor is also specific and differs from the one used in systems running on Freon R12. Use care when working on trim components and use the specified tools correctly in order to avoid damage. PRECAUTIONS The air conditioning circuit uses R134a refrigerant fluid which is environmentally friendly. Closely observe the following safety regulations when working on the circuit: Any R134a fluid which accidentally escapes from the climate control system or the draining/recovery/re-pressurizing equipment can become toxic if very close to naked flames or in the presence of certain metals (for example magnesium or aluminium) in the form of fine particles or powder. It is therefore advisable to work away from naked flames, in well ventilated areas with an exhaust system switched on. Avoid prolonged contact between R134a fluid and skin during the evaporation stage because the low temperature (-26.5° Χ) reached at the end of the expansion can cause cold 'burns'. It is advisable to wear leather or thick fabric gloves. It is vital to protect eyes from contact with the coolant because the extreme low temperature could cause serious injury. Draining the fluid in the open air constitutes a danger to the environment. Only use the special equipment to drain R134a from the system.

Disconnect the Bag connector at the line involved and connect the special line closure resistor. Connect the Examiner to the diagnostic socket. Cancel the errors and check that they have disappeared.
